item.title: Partial $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings: (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$. In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property. In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$. We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations. Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Qingbo Huang

item.title: Modeling and Analysis of Cooling Induced Isotropic Nematic Transitions in Pharmaceutical Liquid Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.00273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the phase transition from an isotropic to a nematic liquid crystal driven by controlled cooling, motivated by the manufacturing of next-generation pharmaceutical drugs. Using the non-isothermal Ericksen model for liquid crystals with a variable degree of orientation, we formulate the problem as a stiff, quasilinear system of parabolic partial differential equations. We establish a consistent thermodynamic framework, prove the well-posedness of the system, and conduct a rigorous asymptotic and numerical scaling analysis of the moving phase boundary in a cylindrical cell subjected to bottom-wall convective cooling. Our analysis identifies a critical sample thickness that separates two distinct physical regimes. Below this threshold, the transition follows the cooling dynamics and the material remains quasi-isothermal. Above the thickness threshold, bulk thermal diffusion governs the dynamics, imposing a dominant thermal delay characterized by a concave quadratic propagation front. These results demonstrate that scaling from laboratory characterization to industrial production fundamentally alters the spatial thermal history of the material, providing a predictive mathematical framework to optimize cooling protocols for kinetic arrest.
item.dc:creator: Pei Liu, Debanjan Banerjee, Daniel Siebel-Cortopassi, Sichen Song, Maria-Carme Calderer

item.title: Fourier analysis on a class of Schwartz spaces and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.00302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The study of regularity and solvability of partial differential operators on non-compact manifolds requires the construction of adapted functional spaces. In this work we introduce $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$, the Schwartz space on the product of a homogeneous space $\mathfrak{M}$ and the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$. We characterize $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ and its topological dual by employing discrete Fourier analysis in terms of eigenfunction expansions associated with a class of anisotropic elliptic operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We provide a characterization via partial Fourier coefficients and via full coefficients, that is, with respect to both components of $\mathfrak{M} \times \mathbb{R}^n$ simultaneously, which is achieved by studying the Fourier analysis on $\mathfrak{M}$. Our results provide new tools for the analysis of operators in this broader setting. As an application, we investigate the global existence and regularity of solutions for a class of partial differential equations on $\mathfrak{M}\times \mathbb{R}^n$.
item.dc:creator: Isadora Vieira Coelho da Silva, Paulo Leandro Dattori da Silva, Michael Ruzhansky

item.title: Beyond the reduced Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation: Singular potential, global well-posedness, and micromagnetic limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.00365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the full nonlinear mean-field Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation in micromagnetics arising from Garanin's spin-polarisation model [D. Garanin. Fokker-Planck and Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equations for classical ferromagnets. Phys. Rev. B, 55 (1997)] prior to the usual near-equilibrium reduction. The equation combines a singular inverse-Langevin potential with a mobility whose longitudinal component degenerates at saturation, together with exchange, anisotropy, and the nonlocal whole-space stray field. The natural state space is the closed unit ball $|m|\leq 1$. For any $H^1$ initial data satisfying $|m_0|\leq1$, including saturated data of infinite free energy, we construct global weak solutions and derive instantaneous separation from saturation $|m|=1$. This restores uniform parabolicity and yields the thermodynamic formulation and exact energy identity for positive times. We further establish a quantitative low-temperature limit to the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation and prove convergence of global trajectories to a single equilibrium. A spectral Curie-type threshold characterises the stability of the paramagnetic state and yields exponential relaxation above the threshold. Finally, for uniformly separated data we prove strong well-posedness, including global strong solutions in one- and two-dimensional domains, and exponential stability of non-degenerate equilibria, with a small-data global theory in three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Agus L. Soenjaya

item.title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term. Factoring out the equilibrium profile associated with the pinning term reduces the problem to the analysis of a weighted Ginzburg--Landau functional. In the extreme type-II regime, we construct locally minimizing vortexless configurations for applied fields extending far beyond the first critical field. We obtain quantitative estimates showing that these configurations remain close, up to gauge transformations, to a Meissner-type state determined by a weighted London problem. We also prove the uniqueness, up to gauge transformations, of the locally minimizing Meissner-type branch within a quantitatively controlled class of local minimizers. A central difficulty is to derive elliptic estimates that remain uniform in the Ginzburg--Landau parameter in the presence of the resulting spatially dependent weight. Under a small-BMO assumption on this weight, we obtain the required regularity and extend to the three-dimensional pinned setting the metastability picture previously established for the homogeneous model.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rom\'an

item.title: Bilinear Strichartz Estimates and Linear Morawetz Estimates for Schr\"odinger Operators with Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.00454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In dimensions three and above, we establish bilinear Strichartz estimates for Schr\"odinger operators with potentials using perturbative arguments and Morawetz estimates. Our approach does not require smallness of the potential. As part of the analysis, we also establish endpoint versions of the bilinear Christ-Kiselev lemma.
item.dc:creator: Bobby Wilson, Xueying Yu

item.title: Some Remarks on the Asymptotic Behavior of Mean Field Games of Controls
item.description: arXiv:2611.00490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the asymptotic behavior of several mean field games of controls. First, in the time-dependent case, we examine the behavior of solutions to discounted mean field games of controls as the discount factor $\lambda$ tends to infinity. Next, we study three stationary models of mean field games of controls, finding that solutions to the first-order discounted problem and the second-order ergodic problem can be obtained from solutions to the second-order discounted problem by taking $\nu \to 0$ and $\lambda \to 0$, respectively. Finally, we investigate the long-time average behavior of solutions to the time-dependent system with no discount, finding that solutions converge to the solution to the second-order ergodic problem as $T \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Jameson Graber, Elizabeth Matter, Kyle Rosengartner

item.title: Ground States of a Coupled Fractional Schr\"{o}dinger System under a Total-Mass Constraint: Complete Classification and Concentration Behavior
item.description: arXiv:2611.00520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a coupled fractional Schr\"{o}dinger system with trapping potentials under a total-mass constraint, in which both the intraspecies and the interspecies interactions are attractive. For every fractional order $s\in(0,1)$ and dimension $N\ge1$, we obtain a complete classification of the existence and non-existence of minimizers: minimizers exist if and only if both intraspecies coefficients lie below the single-component critical mass and the interspecies coupling coefficient lies below an explicit critical threshold $\beta^*$, and no minimizer exists otherwise. The threshold $\beta^*$ is characterized by means of an auxiliary intensity function, which yields a lower bound for the energy functional without invoking a new coupled Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. As the coupling coefficient approaches $\beta^*$, we analyze the concentration behavior. In the one-dimensional half-Laplacian case, the two components are shown to blow up at a common zero of the trapping potentials and, after rescaling, to converge to the same fractional ground-state profile, with the mass ratio determined explicitly by the intraspecies coefficients and the critical mass. For polynomial trapping potentials whose flattest common zero has order $q_0\in(0,1)$, the sharp blow-up rate is established, and both components concentrate simultaneously at the flattest common minimum.
item.dc:creator: Lijun Liu, Jiabin Zuo

item.title: L2-contraction and Asymptotic Stability of Monotone Shock Waves for Cubic and Quartic KdV-Burgers Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear stability of monotone traveling shock waves arising in the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation with a power-law flux, focusing on the cubic and quartic cases p=3 and p=4, respectively, in the presence of both dissipative and dispersive effects. Since shocks connecting distinct end states destroy the integrable structure of the equation, we introduce a slowly varying reference connection to establish global well-posedness for the Cauchy problem in an affine Sobolev space. A key ingredient in the stability analysis is to establish a new two-sided comparison estimate for the derivative of a monotone shock-wave profile. After a monotone coordinate transformation, this estimate allows the viscous dissipation to be compared with the natural vanishing weight arising in a shifted Poincare inequality. Together with an $L^\infty$ bootstrap controlling the higher-order relative-flux terms, this yields a global $L^2$-contraction property modulo a time-dependent shift for sufficiently small $H^1$ perturbations in the admissible parameter regimes. We obtain exponential decay of the shock profile and show asymptotic convergence to the shifted shock in $L^q(\R)$, $2<q\leq \infty$, with vanishing shift velocity.
item.dc:creator: Yi Du, Tao Yan, Yushu Zeng, Shihui Zhu

item.title: Weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates of a generalized Oseen evolution operator in exterior domains, with applications to the Navier-Stokes flow past a rigid body
item.description: arXiv:2611.00649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a generalized Oseen evolution operator arising from time-dependent rigid motions in 3D exterior domains. Hishida and the present author established the regularity theory of the evolution operator by use of the $L^q$-$L^r$ smoothing estimates with a weight function $(1+|x|)^{\alpha}$. The objective of this paper is to develop the weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates globally in time. These estimates are applied to the study of the large time behavior of the Navier-Stokes flow around a time-periodic solution in weighted spaces.
item.dc:creator: Yosuke Asami

item.title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stable regular solutions of the variable-coefficient equation $-\operatorname{div}((A(x)
abla u\cdot
abla u)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u)=f(u)$ in $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, where $p>1$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove quantitative interior H"older estimates for $n<p+4p/(p-1)$ when $p\ge2$, and for $n<5p$ when $1<p<2$. We also obtain interior energy estimates and higher integrability of the gradient in every dimension. These estimates are given in terms of $\|u\|_{L^1(B_1)}$, with constants depending only on $n,p$, the ellipticity bounds, and a local $L^\infty$ bound for $DA$, but not on $f$ or higher derivatives of $A$. These results extend the corresponding interior estimates of Cabr'e, Miraglio, and Sanch'on for the $p$-Laplace equation to this variable-coefficient setting. The proof uses weighted Hessian estimates to control coefficient errors and a comparison between radial and full gradient energies.
item.dc:creator: Weican Luo

item.title: On the unconstrained Allen-Cahn system and its Cahn-Hilliard limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.00778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In [F.P. Duda et al., Meccanica, 2021] the new theory for constituent migration in solids with microstructure was developed. We consider the one-dimensional version of the basic system of this theory with generally non-zero kinetic modulus and the particular diffusivity of the "fast diffusion" type. We obtain exact traveling wave solutions for this system, and analyze several unconstraint and constraint limiting cases. We show that in unconstraint cases of Allen-Cahn type, i.e. for two independent variables, the system demonstrates broader set of possible regimes; in the constraint limit only CH-type process remains.

item.title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.00876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle A\omega,\omega\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
item.description: arXiv:2611.00964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Wenting Huang, Zekai Luo, Ying Sun, Jiahong Wu, Xiaojing Xu

item.title: Decay Rate toward the Rarefaction Wave and the Viscous Contact Wave for Jin--Xin Relaxation Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.00969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes the time-decay rates toward the rarefaction wave and the viscous contact wave for the one-dimensional Jin--Xin relaxation system under the $L^1$ integrability condition of the initial perturbation. In the case of a strictly convex flux, we employ a decomposition method to derive a logarithmic $L^1$ estimate related to a conjecture proposed by Liu\cite{liu2001lp}. Furthermore, a time-weighted $L^2$ method yields the optimal decay rate toward the rarefaction wave. Regarding the case where the flux is partially linearly degenerate, by employing a similar \(L^1\) estimate and time-weighted \(L^2\) method, along with a refined estimate of the nonlinear wave interactions, we obtain the corresponding decay rate toward the composite wave. The decay estimates are obtained without smallness assumptions on the initial perturbations or the wave strength.
item.dc:creator: Mutong He, Feimin Huang, Tianyi Wang, Lingda Xu

item.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
item.description: arXiv:2611.00998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and localized boundary data $\psi(x')\phi(t)\mathbf e_j$, $1\le j\le n$, where $\psi$ is supported in the closed unit ball. A separation point is a boundary point outside $\operatorname{supp}\psi$ where a component takes both signs on positive-measure sets in every sufficiently small adjoining space-time neighborhood. By evaluating the spatial convolutions appearing in the solution formula of the Stokes system via confluent hypergeometric functions, we obtain explicit formulas for the first normal derivatives of tangential components, the second normal derivative of the normal component, and tangential pressure derivatives at the boundary. For normal data, suitable H\"{o}lder regularity and strict log-concavity of $\phi$ yield a unique separation point for each tangential component at every point of its coordinate axis outside the ball, and exactly two for the normal component at each sufficiently distant boundary point. We prove monotonicity and large-distance asymptotics of their temporal coordinates and quantitative temporal vanishing estimates for the normal derivatives. For tangential data in $n\ge3$, we prove the existence and uniqueness of separation points of tangential and normal components, including at fixed spatial points while $\phi$ is positive. We derive spatial asymptotics at large distance and time from data moments and, under a geometric condition, supporting faces of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$. We characterize tangential pressure-gradient signs for both tangential and normal data, locating favorable and adverse regions near the boundary. For radial $\psi$, additional assumptions yield existence, uniqueness, and asymptotics of pressure-gradient zeros and zero curves, including those governed by the zero of the Caputo half-derivative of $\phi$.
item.dc:creator: Chanhong Min, Kyungkeun Kang

item.title: Global classical solutions of the repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2611.01004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global classical existence for general large data in the three-dimensional repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system has long been an open problem. We give an affirmative answer: every nonnegative $C^1$ initial datum satisfying \[ f_0(x,p)+|\nabla_{x,p}f_0(x,p)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-a}\langle p\rangle^{-b},\qquad a>1,\quad b>3, \] generates a unique global classical solution. No smallness or symmetry is assumed. The result covers finite and infinite mass and energy, including infinite kinetic energy density. The power thresholds are sharp for general pure-power bounds ensuring finite density and an absolutely convergent Coulomb field. The proof rests on two new mechanisms: local energy recovery for a population selected by energy growth, and a corrected moment--action closure based on nonnegative transverse interactions. The argument also yields global classical solutions of the nonrelativistic equation in the same initial class, allowing infinite mass with polynomial velocity tails of any order $b>3$.
item.dc:creator: Feimin Huang, Jingpeng Wu, Hang Xiong

item.title: Ground state uniqueness and quantitative stability for the mass-critical Hartree equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.01013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the ground state of the mass-critical Hartree equation is unique up to phase rotations and translations and nondegenerate in every dimension $d\ge3$. This makes the recent conditional $L^2$ classification of minimal-mass blow-up and non-scattering solutions unconditional; we also give a direct $H^1$ proof of the finite-time blow-up classification. We further establish a global quadratic stability estimate for the sharp Hartree interpolation inequality. For the optimal stability constant, we rule out vanishing of minimizing sequences and describe their possible loss of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Inverse source problem of variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates an inverse temporal source problem for a variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equation with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. By the perturbation method, the model is equivalently transformed into a constant-order fractional diffusion equation with a convolution perturbation term. Existence, uniqueness, and energy estimates of strong and weak solutions to the forward problem are established, and for a separable source term the uniqueness and Lipschitz stability of the temporal source function are proved using local integral observations. A numerical reconstruction algorithm combining Tikhonov regularization with the conjugate gradient method is developed with a convergence error estimate, and numerical experiments verify its effectiveness and stability for different variable-exponent functions, noise levels and source functions. Since fractional advection--diffusion models describe the turbulent transport of airborne pollutants, the method is also applicable in atmospheric science for recovering the emission history of a pollution source from sparse measurements.
item.dc:creator: Li Hu, Zhiyuan Li, Zhidong Zhang

item.title: Stability of least-energy solutions of the harmonic map flow from the plane into the 2-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.01021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of the least-energy harmonic map $W:\mathbb R^2\to S^2$ for the harmonic map flow under small, sufficiently decaying, non-symmetric perturbations. Solutions exist globally and are asymptotically described by a modulation of $W$ plus a remainder that converges to zero as $t\to\infty$. The modulation parameters associated with scaling, rotation, and translation remain close to their initial values and converge to finite limits. The proof relies on an inner-outer gluing decomposition and the analysis of a non-local equation governing the modulation parameters.
item.dc:creator: Juan Davila, Eliott Van Steirteghem

item.title: Far-field Layers of Steady State for Viscous and Heat-conductive Gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.01026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the vanishing heat conductivity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions to the non-isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the exterior of a ball under an inflow boundary condition. A distinctive feature of this singular limit is the formation of a far-field layer whose transition region moves toward spatial infinity as the heat conductivity tends to zero. We establish the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions with the uniform estimates with respect to the heat conductivity and analyze the corresponding limiting problem. The limiting solution generally fails to attain the prescribed far-field density and temperature separately, although its pressure at infinity agrees with the prescribed far-field pressure. We show that this discrepancy gives rise to a far-field layer, derive its explicit representation, and identify its characteristic spatial scale. Finally, we prove that the stationary solution is uniformly approximated over the entire exterior domain by the superposition of the limiting solution and the far-field layer.
item.dc:creator: Akitaka Matsumura, Masahiro Suzuki

item.title: Nonlinear kink modes for nonisentropic supersonic vortex sheets
item.description: arXiv:2611.01036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, planar nonisentropic vortex sheets of the two-dimensional Euler equations under the stability condition are studied via nonlinear geometric optics, focusing on the interaction induced by a small-amplitude, high-frequency incident wave impinging on a planar vortex sheet. It is found that there exist three asymmetric critical incident angles at which resonance occurs, leading to a significant amplification of the reflected and refracted oscillatory waves. Moreover, by refining the asymptotic expansion, we deduce that the leading profiles of the highly oscillatory waves are described by initial-boundary value problems for Burgers transport equations, while the leading profile of the contact discontinuity front satisfies an initial value problem for a Hamilton--Jacobi-type equation, which reduces to a forced linear transport equation on one resonant branch. These results extend the resonant amplification mechanism from the isentropic setting to the nonisentropic Euler flow and reveal the asymmetric influence of entropy variations on the nonlinear evolution of compressible vortex sheets.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Li, Yang Xu

item.title: Impact Mechanism of a Point Interaction in the Cubic Half-Wave Equation: Well-Posedness, Constrained Energy Levels and Near-Critical Rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.01041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear half-wave equation with a logarithmically renormalized point interaction. The nonlinearity is focusing and cubic, which is mass-critical. We establish well-posedness in the energy space using a new method for unconditional uniqueness that requires no auxiliary Strichartz assumption. We reveal the mechanism by which the point interaction affects ground states. The free critical mass is the sharp threshold: fixed-mass ground states exist and are orbitally stable below it, whereas at and above it the constrained energy is unbounded from below. We also prove a near-critical rigidity result showing that bounded energy concentrating sequences converge to free ground states after rescaling.
item.dc:creator: Xingkai Ju, Yuanhong Wei

item.title: Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD
item.description: arXiv:2611.01124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.
item.dc:creator: Yinghui Wang

item.title: Local and global conservation laws of partial differential equations on moving domains in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For PDE systems in three spatial dimensions, firstly, a review of the various types of global conservation laws --- volumetric, surface-flux, circulatory --- is given using vector calculus, and their corresponding local forms --- divergence, curl, gradient --- are explained. Secondly, an extension of each type of conservation law to moving domains is presented, where the domain --- volume, surface, curve --- is transported by a prescribed velocity field. This provides a generalization of Reynolds' transport theorem known for material domains in which the velocity field is the fluid velocity. The main results are illustrated by numerous physical examples taken from gas dynamics, fluid flow, nonlinear acoustics, chemotaxis, plasma dynamics, and also Maxwell's equations, which do not involve any physically specified velocity field. As an additional main result, an extension of the multiplier method for finding local conservation laws of divergence-type is presented for local curl-type and gradient-type conservation laws on both static and moving domains.
item.dc:creator: Alexey F. Shevyakov, Stephen C. Anco

item.title: A Game of Scales
item.description: arXiv:2611.01142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes cover the material of two courses given at SISSA, Trieste, in the academic years 2023-2024 and 2025-2026, together with some material from courses taught in other recent years. The original idea behind these courses emerged from conversations with Andrea Causin and Margherita Solci about the somewhat elusive notion of `multiscale behaviour', which arises in the study of variational problems involving one or more small parameters. Two main mechanisms govern their asymptotic behaviour: concentration and oscillations. Their description is often associated with the emergence of a characteristic `scale', quantifying either the speed of concentration or the period of an optimal oscillation. These mechanisms may originate from different variational principles and may occur separately, coexist, compete, or interact, thus providing a natural interpretation of the term `multiscale'. This perspective inspired the informal title of the courses, which also became the title of these notes. The natural framework for these analyses is $\Gamma$-convergence. However, these notes are not intended as a general introduction to this now well-established theory. We provide only a brief account of the techniques relevant to our purposes, referring the reader to the author's book chapter {\em A Handbook of $\Gamma$-convergence}. For a broader introduction to $\Gamma$-convergence, and in particular to its topological properties, the standard reference is Dal Maso's monograph {\em An Introduction to $\Gamma$-convergence}.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Braides

item.title: The Lorentz Threshold in Fourier Restriction
item.description: arXiv:2611.01232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Stein--Tomas restriction controls a Fourier transform on a curved surface, but the estimate changes when its values lie in a Banach space. We determine the sharp Lorentz threshold at the critical exponent $4/3$: for coefficients in $\ell_D^{4/3,q}$, the optimal Gaussian restriction constant grows like $(1+\log D)^{|3/4-1/q|}$. A multiscale wave-packet construction proves sharpness, including the delicate index $q=2$. The same threshold holds for fractional Gaussian noise, while Gaussian type and cotype alone do not distinguish the positive and negative cases. As a dispersive consequence, we establish a sharp Lorentz-channel spacetime estimate for linear capillary waves.
item.dc:creator: R. Shahmurov, V. Shahmurov

item.title: $a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
item.description: arXiv:2611.01258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result was subsequently extended to composite planar waves for general $n\times n$ viscous systems in arbitrary spatial dimensions. The present paper is a companion to that work. Here we prove the estimates on viscous shock profiles needed to apply $a$-contraction with shifts, including derivative estimates that go beyond the standard bounds. We also give a streamlined account of the main ideas of the method by focusing on a single viscous shock for a general one-dimensional system.
item.dc:creator: Young-Sam Kwon, Jiayun Meng, Alexis Vasseur

item.title: Heat flow and the fundamental solution of the Baouendi-Grushin operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.01336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the Baouendi-Grushin operator $\mathscr L_\gamma = \Delta_x + |x|^{2\gamma}\Delta_y$ in $\R^{m+k}$, with $\gamma>0$, we prove that the time integral of the heat kernel with pole at the origin equals $C_{\gamma,Q}\, N_\gamma^{2-Q}$, where $N_\gamma$ is the gauge and $Q$ the homogeneous dimension. When $\gamma\not=1$ no closed form of the heat kernel is known. After a partial Fourier transform in $y$, the time integral of the heat kernel becomes the Green function of an anharmonic oscillator, which solves a generalized modified Bessel equation, and the gauge appears when the inverse Fourier transform is computed as a Hankel transform. In particular, the heat flow provides a new proof that $C_{\gamma,Q}\, N_\gamma^{2-Q}$ is a fundamental solution of $-\mathscr L_\gamma$ with pole at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Garofalo

item.title: Strict rearrangement inequalities for logarithmic p-Laplacians
item.description: arXiv:2611.01366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish cases of equality for the Polya-Szego inequality of the logarithmic p-Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Hichem Hajaiej, Qinyang Li, Weichang Zhan

item.title: Exponential stability of the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature
item.description: arXiv:2611.01381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the reduced Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin system with one temperature, obtained from the full Bresse--Gurtin--Pipkin thermoelastic beam system by neglecting one of the two temperature variables. This system was left essentially open in a recent work of Dell'Oro, where only a conjecture on its exponential stability condition was formulated. By combining the spectral analysis recently developed by Dell'Oro, Pata and Vasylyeva for the abstract Gurtin--Pipkin heat equation with the resolvent estimate framework of Dell'Oro for Bresse systems, we prove that the associated contraction semigroup is exponentially stable if and only if two explicit stability numbers, depending on the structural constants of the beam, both vanish. The proof is based on a spectral characterization of the infinitesimal generator in a half-plane containing the imaginary axis, an analysis of its spectrum on the imaginary axis, sharp upper bounds for the resolvent, and the Gearhart--Pr\"uss theorem. In particular, we confirm the conjecture of Dell'Oro and provide a rigorous spectral analysis of the reduced system. The same method yields the exponential stability characterization of the corresponding reduced Bresse--Maxwell--Cattaneo system, and can be adapted to other reduced Bresse-type models.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhou

item.title: Continuity of Global Attractors under a Mass-Preserving Singular Memory Limit, with an Application to a Coupled Suspension Bridge System
item.description: arXiv:2611.01388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the global attractor of a dissipative evolution equation with memory depends on the memory kernel when the kernel concentrates, while preserving its total mass, towards a Dirac mass at the origin. The mass-preserving rescaling is the structural feature that prevents the effective elastic coefficients from degenerating in the limit, so that the memory-dependent dynamics reduces formally to a memoryless damped system with unchanged elastic coefficients. For a coupled nonlinear suspension bridge system with past history, taken as a concrete model, we establish uniform-in-parameter dissipativity and uniform-in-parameter exponential stability of the associated linear semigroup. These uniform estimates yield uniform quasi-stability, uniform exponential attraction, finite-time convergence of the semigroups, and uniform H\"older continuity with respect to the perturbation parameter. We deduce upper semicontinuity of the global attractors, and, under an additional structural stability hypothesis on the limit attractor, lower semicontinuity as well. The analysis separates the general continuity mechanism, which applies to a broad class of memory kernels and dissipative systems, from the model-specific verification, which exploits the coupled bridge structure.
item.dc:creator: Jun Zhou

item.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.01403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<\beta<8\pi$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $\beta<6\pi$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $\beta<8\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru F. Radu

item.title: $L^1$ amplification near a self-similar vortex collapse in 2D Navier-Stokes
item.description:
arXiv:2611.01433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative $L^1$ instability for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse as viscosity tends to zero. For every $0<\gamma< rac12$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, we construct solutions that are $O(
u^{1-\gamma})$-close in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ at $t_0$ but exhibit order-one $L^1$ separation in a shrinking neighborhood of the collapse point at times approaching collapse as $
u	o0$. By time translation, we also obtain pairs of solutions with initial $L^1$ distance $O(
u^{1-\gamma})$ that develop order-one separation at a fixed positive time. In both constructions, the solutions have the same viscosity and total circulation and are uniformly bounded in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The proof exploits the amplification of small time delays, the fast speed of the vortex centers near collapse, together with sharp inviscid approximation estimates for the Navier--Stokes equations established in~\cite{Ga11,NguyenCollapse}.
item.dc:creator: Trinh T. Nguyen

item.title: Almost global solutions of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains without the second null condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.01471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For 3-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and small initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$, the authors of two papers [M. Keel, H. Smith, C.D. Sogge, Amer. J. Math. 122 (2000), no. 4, 805-842; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004), no. 1, 109-153] have shown that the lifespan ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions satisfies ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ or ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon}$, depending on whether the null condition holds or not, respectively. However, for the corresponding 2-D problem in exterior domains, it remains a difficult and unsolved problem to determine the precise lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions. In our previous papers, we have established that $T_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ holds when both the first and second null conditions are satisfied; and that $T_{\varepsilon}\ge\frac{C}{\varepsilon^2}$ holds when the first null condition is violated. In this paper, we will prove $T_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon^2}$ when the first null condition holds but the second null condition is violated. Combining these results, we have systematically established sharp estimates for the lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moreover, our series of results for quasilinear wave equations in 2-D exterior domains are consistent with the corresponding results for the classical Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Fei Hou, Huicheng Yin

item.title: Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
item.description: arXiv:2611.01479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $\lambda$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-\lambda t$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.
item.dc:creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Antonios Zitridis

item.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -\Delta u+u=\lambda u\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<\lambda<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: Spontaneous Geometric Structures in 2D MHD Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.01579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under suitable spatial decay assumptions on the initial data, we establish precise asymptotic expansions of the velocity and magnetic fields for two-dimensional incompressible MHD flows at each positive time. We identify in the far-field profile the hexagonal pattern previously discovered for the 2D Navier-Stokes equations by L. Brandolese \cite{Bra22}, characterized by six equally spaced directions of faster decay for each component of $u(x,t)-u_0(x)$. Surprisingly, the corresponding contribution to the magnetic field vanishes identically, owing to an exact cancellation associated with the antisymmetric structure of the magnetic nonlinearity. Thus, at order $|x|^{-3}$, the hexagonal structure appears only in the velocity field.
item.dc:creator: Matheus Nasi, Cilon F. Perusato

item.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions and H\"{o}lder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Orbital stability for the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.01596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For equivariance index $m\ge2$ and a potential $V\in C^{3,1}([0,2])$ satisfying $V(0)=V'(0)=0$, we first establish local well-posedness for the Cauchy problem at the $H^2$ level, with the sphere constraint written in the natural affine space $u-\vec n\in H^2$. For nonnegative $V$ we then consider an $m$--equivariant ground state of $H_\omega=E+\omega M$, $\omega>0$. Under a constrained nondegeneracy condition for the polar Hessian, the conserved energy and mass give orbital stability in $H^1$. A Gustafson--Shatah type continuation argument, in which the Chern--Simons feedback is treated as a tame nonlocal zeroth-order perturbation, upgrades this conditional stability to global $H^2$ existence for all $H^2$ initial data sufficiently close to the ground state orbit in $H^1$. For the quadratic potential we also verify the nondegeneracy condition in a nonempty interior near-BPS regime approaching the self-dual point $(\kappa,\omega)=(1,0)$. This yields a concrete family of globally defined orbitally stable ground states.
item.dc:creator: Guanghui Jin, Jinmyoung Seok, Jianjun Yuan

item.title: Logarithmic Sobolev and exponential inequalities for submanifolds in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for complete $C^{1,1}$ immersed submanifolds of dimension $m\ge2$ in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with sectional curvature at most $-b^2$. The inequality retains the Euclidean sharp constant after subtraction of $(m-1)^2b^2$ from the Fisher and mean-curvature energy; this coefficient is maximal for a lower bound uniform over $b\ge0$. For immersed surfaces, we prove both a finite-domain critical exponential inequality and a global Ruf-type inequality with a positive $L^2$ term. Both have potential $|H|^2-b^2$, exponent $16\pi$ and an absolute multiplicative constant, and follow from one geometric heat-kernel comparison. The exponent and curvature coefficient are optimal. We classify Gaussian equality in the logarithmic inequality and geometric equality in the higher-dimensional Nash consequence. All inequality constants are independent of the codimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
item.description: arXiv:2611.01616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.
item.dc:creator: Avetik Arakelyan, Davit Alaverdyan, Naira Hovakimyan, Isaac Kaminer, Tigran Bakaryan

item.title: Chern scalar curvature and finite-time singularities of the conformal Chern--Calabi flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.01623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On every unit-volume flat complex three-torus, we construct a solution of the volume-preserving conformal Chern--Calabi flow with a finite-time Chern Type-I singularity at any prescribed point. The full spatial supremum has an exact asymptotic coefficient, and prescribed rescalings converge to a complete nonflat radial shrinking solution. The positive part of Chern scalar curvature can remain arbitrarily small throughout the flow, as can each prescribed subcritical spatial curvature norm. We determine the punctured terminal metric, its one-point completion and unique nonflat tangent cone, and the terminal energy asymptotics. We also exclude Chern Type-II under a logarithmically improved critical weak $L^3$ bound on Chern scalar curvature, and prove a separate scale-invariant integral criterion involving first Chern--Ricci curvature. The constructed singular solutions satisfy both criteria.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: Spectral Exactness and Quantitative Instability Approximation in the Euler-Zeitlin Model for Zonal Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.01664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on finite-time convergence results for geometric matrix hydrodynamics, we establish global spectral exactness for Zeitlin's approximation of the two-dimensional Euler equation on the sphere linearized about polynomial zonal vorticities. By separating each azimuthal block into a skew-adjoint transport operator and a compact perturbation, we obtain a dimension-uniform estimate $\|K_N-K\|=O(N^{-1})$ and the sharper fixed-block estimate $\|K_{N,m}-K_m\|=O(N^{-2})$. These bounds, together with strong-resolvent convergence of transport, yield exact approximation of the isolated spectrum off the imaginary axis: algebraic multiplicities are preserved, Riesz projections converge in norm, and spurious off-axis spectral limits are excluded. Every algebraically simple off-axis eigenvalue has an $O(N^{-2})$ approximation error. For eigenvalues of higher multiplicity we establish second-order convergence of arithmetic means of eigenvalue clusters and $O(N^{-2/\alpha})$ individual eigenvalue bounds, where $\alpha$ is the maximal Jordan-block size. For any prescribed positive growth margin, the numbers of unstable and stable eigenvalues beyond that margin are eventually correct. The argument combines an exact matrix-harmonic coordinate recurrence, uniform bounds for high azimuthal modes, and resolvent factorizations involving compact operators. An explicit degree-three zonal equilibrium has a rigorously enclosed simple unstable eigenvalue, providing a concrete instance of the quantitative theory.
item.dc:creator: Robert Vrabel

item.title: Generalized Principal Eigenvalues of Spatially Periodic Nonlocal Operators with Applications to Noncooperative KPP Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study generalized principal eigenvalues of the spatially periodic cooperative nonlocal operator $\mathcal{L}\boldsymbol{\varphi}=\mathcal{J}*\boldsymbol{\varphi} -\boldsymbol{\varphi}+A(x)\boldsymbol{\varphi}$ and their applications to noncooperative KPP systems. In the periodic setting, we characterize the existence of a classical principal eigenvalue and explicitly construct and classify Radon measure solutions to the associated eigenproblem when a positive continuous principal eigenfunction does not exist. On the whole space, we consider two notions of generalized principal eigenvalues defined through positive test functions and characterize them through a family of weighted periodic spectral values and Dirichlet approximations. For large spatial periods, we identify the spectral limits through a scalar Hamilton--Jacobi cell problem and, under additional assumptions, derive leading-order corrections and eigenfunction concentration results. For small spatial periods, we characterize the limits by an averaged operator and obtain refined expansions for specific classes of kernels, including formulas for the difference between the two whole-space generalized principal eigenvalues. Finally, we apply the spectral theory to establish extinction and persistence criteria for the associated noncooperative KPP systems, characterize spreading speeds along rays by a Freidlin--G\"artner-type formula, and study their asymptotic behavior as the spatial period tends to infinity or zero.
item.dc:creator: Hoang-Hung Vo, Ming-Zhen Xin

item.title: Chaotic Dynamics of Charged Particles in Magnetic Fields with Singular Forces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study charged-particle dynamics under a non-Lipschitz velocity-dependent force with magnetic and damping effects, focusing on continuation through zero velocity and chaos in the velocity direction. For a time-independent directional force and fixed parameters, we introduce a $C^1$ regularization. When an unregularized trajectory reaches zero velocity in finite time, inner rescaling yields convergence to a reference orbit within the regularization ball, while the regularized trajectories converge locally uniformly outside it to a unique continuation. For the directional dynamics, stereographic projection yields a parameterized Euclidean system. By choosing the skew-symmetric magnetic part, we obtain a nonautonomous parameterized center manifold reduction with a prescribed finite Taylor jet. Under an additional factorization assumption, the reduced dynamics admits Shilnikov homoclinic orbits and associated chaos.
item.dc:creator: Linhao Chen, Yong Li, Weiping Yan

item.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
item.description: arXiv:2611.01738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. In particular we develop an observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. In particular, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. We provide an explicit easy-to-implement observer design guaranteeing convergence. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of same dispersive water-wave models.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Neeraje, Vishal Vasan

item.title: Uniqueness results for the exterior Dirichlet and Neumann problem in two dimensions for the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with linear growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.01780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider solutions $u, v:\Omega\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{N}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equations associated to the variational integral $\int_{\Omega}f(\nabla u)dx$, where $\Omega$ is an exterior domain in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ e.g., the complement of a disk or a half plane, and the density $f$ is of linear growth. Among other things we show that $u|_{\partial\Omega}=v|_{\partial\Omega}$ together with the boundedness of $u-v$ yields that $u=v$ on the entire domain.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bildhauer Martin Fuchs

item.title: Lehto-type growth conditions and a Picard theorem for the gradient of entire solutions to the Euler -- Lagrange equations of variational integrals with linear growth in the plane including a small extension of Moser's Bernstein result
item.description:
arXiv:2611.01784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We mainly consider entire solutions $u: \mathbb{R}^2 ightarrow \mathbb{R}$ of the Euler -- Lagrange equation for a variational integral with density $g(|
abla u|)$ of linear growth. Assuming a Lehto-type condition at infinity, we show that either $
abla u$ is a constant vector or the image of $
abla u$ is the whole plane with the possible exception of at most one point. This result is extended to certain energy densities of nearly linear growth. Moreover, we slightly generalize the Bernstein result of Moser.
item.dc:creator: Martin Fuchs

item.title: Global weak solutions with vacuum for isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the unit disk under Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct global weak solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes and Navier-Stokes-Poisson systems in the unit disk under no-slip boundary conditions, allowing vacuum and unbounded densities for sufficiently small initial energy. Such solutions particularly possess uniform $L^{q_0}$ density bounds for some $q_0>4\gamma$, beyond the natural energy class. Our analysis combines Green function representations with the mean-value property of harmonic functions to isolate a pressure-generated harmonic component of the effective viscous flux and obtain a purely interior potential representation valid for both systems. These results complement Perepelitsa's half-space theory (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 212 (2014), pp. 709-726) and our recent half-plane work (arXiv:2601.11852, 2026), treating bounded-domain geometry and Poisson coupling with nonnegative initial density.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Wang, Xin Zhong

item.title: Periodic Fisher-KPP equations on a regular tree
item.description: arXiv:2611.01842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fisher-KPP equations on regular trees with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in distance from a vertex or a bi-infinite geodesic. For nonzero finitely supported data, we characterize the spectral threshold between uniform extinction and persistence, including critical extinction. We establish Bramson corrections for Busemann step data at positive, zero and negative speeds and, above the periodic extinction threshold, for the largest Busemann coordinate and radial level positions of finitely supported solutions. When the periodic spectral minimum is nonpositive but the geodesic spectral threshold is positive, we construct a smallest positive stationary solution with exponential transverse decay, prove uniqueness under an exponential bound, and determine longitudinal spreading with its logarithmic correction. We also classify positive stationary solutions depending only on distance from the geodesic and prove existence and stability results for moving and stationary fronts.
item.dc:creator: Yuanyang Hu

item.title: Chemotaxis-Stokes system with $p$-Laplacian slow diffusion: global boundedness across the full $p>2$ range
item.description: arXiv:2611.01847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The global boundedness problem for three-dimensional chemotaxis-fluid systems with nonlinear diffusion presents substantial analytical challenges, particularly in the near-linear diffusion regime. Indeed, the porous-medium and p-Laplacian diffusion operators approach the classical Laplacian as $m\searrow1$ and $p\searrow2$, and the extra a priori control afforded by nonlinear structures becomes increasingly difficult to exploit. This difficulty is reflected in the porous-medium setting, where establishing boundedness throughout $m>1$ required a sequence of substantial developments spanning more than a decade (2010-2024). For the p-Laplacian case, despite significant progress, the problem remained open in the near-linear range $2<p\le p^*(\approx2.01)$, due to the saturation of classical Moser-type iterations as $p\searrow2$. In this paper, we establish global bounded strong solutions for a three-dimensional chemotaxis-Stokes system with p-Laplacian slow diffusion and signal consumption. Our approach departs from the conventional $L^q$-iteration framework and develops a weighted energy method that directly exploits the coercive structure of the nonlinear diffusion operator. A weighted Rellich identity yields density estimates. To control the resulting boundary contribution on general smooth domains, we first use tangential differentiation along the boundary to lower its order, and then apply a trace-embedding estimate. Combined with a high-gradient/low-gradient decomposition, these estimates allow us to control the mixed chemotactic terms and close the coupled estimates for the density, signal, and fluid. The resulting estimates hold throughout $2<p\le 3$, thereby resolving the previously open range $2<p\le p^*$. Together with existing results for $p>p^*$, our work establishes boundedness throughout the entire slow-diffusion range $p>2$.
item.dc:creator: Chunhua Jin

item.title: Dynamics of solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation on a $\mathcal{Y}$-junction
item.description: arXiv:2611.01856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time behavior of solutions to the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a Y-junction, a metric graph consisting of one incoming and two outgoing half-lines joined at a vertex. We first identify vertex conditions of separating-derivative type, together with a balance between the nonlinear coefficients and the coupling parameters, under which the problem is globally well-posed in $L^2$ for arbitrarily large data. This regime coincides with the one in which the explicit solitary waves of the junction, recently constructed by Mugnolo, Noja and Seifert (2025), exist. Using virial inequalities in the spirit of Mu\~noz and Ponce (2019), we then establish decay, in the sense of liminf, of the $L^2$ norm of the solution in time-dependent regions far from the solitons. In the strongly dominated linear region, which moves away from the vertex, the three edges decouple and the decay holds for every admissible choice of parameters. In the weakly dominated linear region, which stays close to the vertex, the topology of the graph produces boundary contributions at the vertex, and the decay is obtained under an algebraic condition on the coupling parameters that makes these contributions cancel. Finally, we discuss adaptations to general star graphs.
item.dc:creator: M\'arcio Cavalcante, Nicola de Nitti

item.title: On $W^{2,1}$-Regularity for Rivi\`ere's System with a Local Hardy Drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.01877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the endpoint regularity of weak solutions to the inhomogeneous Rivi\`ere system $$ -\Delta u=\Omega\cdot\nabla u+f \qquad\text{in }B_1\subset\mathbb R^2, $$ with an antisymmetric potential $\Omega\in L^2$ and a local Hardy drift term $f\in h^1$. We construct a continuous solution in $W_0^{1,2}$, which fails to belong to $W^{2,1}$ in every neighborhood of the origin, even when $\|\Omega\|_{L^2}$ is arbitrarily small. Smooth truncations further show that the corresponding uniform interior $W^{2,1}$ estimate fails even for smooth solutions and coefficients. Thus, the $L\log L$ assumption ensuring local $W^{2,1}$ regularity cannot in general be replaced by componentwise local Hardy data.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Ting Kang, Wen-Juan Qi, Zhao-Min Sun

item.title: Generalized Hamiltonian gradient flow of contact type II: singularities, cut locus, and controllability
item.description: arXiv:2611.01911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study singularities, cut loci and controllability for time-dependent contact Hamilton--Jacobi equations. A contact version of Arnaud's theorem identifies the superdifferential graph of an evolved profile with the contact Hamiltonian image of the differential graph of its positive Lax--Oleinik regularization. This representation defines intrinsic singular characteristics and determines their initial velocity through a minimum-energy selection on the space-time superdifferential. The curves are continuous and locally $1/2$-H\"older, but they need not be locally Lipschitz. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal even for a quadratic Hamiltonian. The intrinsic characteristic issued from a cut point is singular at every later time in the short-time interval. We also establish the contact Lax--Oleinik commutator identities, which identify the superlevel and sublevel sets of the cut time with the corresponding terminal momentum graphs through bi-Lipschitz maps. For reachable terminal data we characterize the associated calibrated sets, and we describe all continuous initial data that reach a prescribed semiconcave profile. The proofs use Herglotz' variational principle and short-time estimates for contact fundamental solutions.
item.dc:creator: Qingyang Cai, Wei Cheng, Tianqi Shi

item.title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Yuming Qin, Junchen Liu

item.title: Time-Decay Rates toward Rarefaction Waves for the One-Dimensional Isentropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations has been well established since the pioneering works of Matsumura--Nishihara \cite{MatsumuraNishihara1986} and Liu--Xin \cite{LiuXin1988}, the classical $L^2$ energy method yields only qualitative convergence in $L^\infty(\R)$ as $t\to\infty$ without any explicit decay rate. In this paper, we establish for the first time a standalone \(L^4\) energy estimate for perturbations of a weak rarefaction wave in the one-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system, thereby obtaining the first explicit algebraic time-decay rates for this model. Specifically, for small initial perturbations in $H^2(\R)$ and small wave strength $\delta$, we prove that $(v-V,u-U)$ decays in $L^4(\R)$ at the rate \[ \|(v-V,u-U)(t)\|_{L^4}\le C\bigl(\|(v_0-V(0),u_0-U(0))\|_{H^2}+\sqrt{\delta}\bigr)(1+t)^{-1/8}, \] where \((V,U)\) denotes the smooth rarefaction wave, while the relative Riemann invariants \(z_\pm\) of the perturbed system decay in \(L^\infty(\R)\) at the rate \((1+t)^{-1/6}\). The proof relies on a new local quartic energy estimate for \(z_\pm\) and \(z_\pm-Q\), where \(Q=\mu(v)v_x-\mu(V)V_x\), as well as a nonlocal half-space wave-interaction functional for corrected characteristic modes and a weighted higher-order derivative energy estimate coupled at the scale of the one-dimensional Nash inequality.
item.dc:creator: Mutong He, Feimin Huang, Lingjun Liu, Lingda Xu

item.title: Liouville theorem for monotone solutions of the Lane-Emden system in a half-space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lane-Emden system is an important model case of Hamitonian elliptic systems. We here consider the zero-Dirichlet problem in a half-space for arbitrary powers $p,q\ge1$. We prove that any nonnegative classical solution that is nondecreasing in the normal direction is necessarily trivial. No bound at infinity of any kind is assumed and this extends the known scalar monotonicity theorem. We also obtain the same conclusion for the scalar equation $-\Delta u=f(u)$ when $f\in C^1([0,\infty))$ is nonnegative, $f(0)=0$, $f\not\equiv0$, and $f(s)/s$ is nondecreasing for $s>0$. This relaxes the convexity and $C^2$ regularity requirements on $f$ in previous works. To prove these results we introduce a new method, completely different from the normal convexity approach from previous works, which relies on a delicate combination of techniques and could be applied to more general systems. Our basic tool is a suitable average of the linear interpolant between the solution and its normal limit on each finite strip. We next use stability estimates, combined with an energy argument for the scalar equation, or a contraction argument relying on Bessel potentials and the Schur test for the system. Increasing the strip height then forces the solution to vanish.
item.dc:creator: Yimei Li, Philippe Souplet

item.title: A Unified Space-Time Variational Framework for Wave Equations on Differential Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit a standard space--time variational formulation of the scalar wave equation in the setting of differential forms. For this, we use as spatial operator the nonnegative, self-adjoint (relative) \emph{Hodge--Laplacian} on a bounded Lipschitz domain. Its spectral decomposition reduces the wave problem in any form degree to the same family of scalar ordinary differential equations that underlies existing space-time analysis. We illustrate how this can be used to transfer results from the scalar wave equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to other wave-type problems. In particular, we connect the framework to perfectly electrically conducting Maxwell problems.
item.dc:creator: C. Urz\'ua-Torres, A. Wisse

item.title: Uniqueness and radial symmetry of magnetic skyrmions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness of magnetic skyrmions as global minimizers of the simplest local micromagnetic energy. The strategy is to show that any radial critical point with strictly decreasing out-of-plane component is the unique minimizer in the class of general degree-one maps with the prescribed limit at infinity. To this end, we identify a class of null Lagrangians that is sufficiently flexible to contain a calibration, giving a uniform lower bound for the energy that is uniquely saturated on the critical point. Our arguments provide a blueprint for proofs of symmetry and uniqueness of minimizers in vectorial variational problems under topological constraints.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Di Fratta, Cyrill B. Muratov, Theresa M. Simon, Valeriy V. Slastikov

item.title: Weak and Sharp Stretched-Exponential Flocking in the Kinetic Cucker-Smale Model with Noncompactly Supported Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.02232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model under initial data with unbounded support in both position and velocity. Such data invalidate classical diameter-based flocking arguments and make sustained spatial cohesion difficult to establish. We prove an estimate for spatial characteristics under a finite spatial second moment and a sufficiently high velocity moment, without any requirement on coupling strength. We also prove weak flocking, i.e. control of spatial variance and integrability of velocity fluctuations in time. Under stronger assumptions on the initial tails, we establish uniform propagation of spatial exponential moments of explicitly determined order, a substantially stronger conclusion than bounded spatial variance. These estimates lead to explicit stretched-exponential rates of velocity alignment and convergence of the centered spatial distribution toward a limiting profile. Another contribution is the construction of countably atomic solutions that show optimality of the decay exponent in the spatial-tail-limited class. Together, the results clarify how initial phase-space tails govern spatial confinement and quantitative flocking for kinetic distributions without compact support.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Markou

item.title: Near-Critical Asymptotics and Radial Sharpness for a Two-Weight Hardy Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.02328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal constant $C(p,\gamma)$ in a planar two-weight Hardy inequality relating the gradient and Hessian of a scalar potential, posed by Maz'ya in [14, Problem 3.11]. For every $1\le p<\infty$, we prove \[ \lim_{\gamma\to\gamma_c} 2^{p/2}|\gamma-\gamma_c|^p C(p,\gamma)=1, \qquad \gamma_c=1-\frac2p. \] The proof reduces the curl-free constraint to an angular minimization problem and yields qualitative rigidity of almost extremizers for $p>1$. Moreover, we determine the sharp constant in the radial class for every $1\le p<\infty$ and $\gamma\ne\gamma_c$, thereby resolving the radial case of Maz'ya's problem. We also show that the radial inequality remains valid at $\gamma=\gamma_c$, with the same sharp constant \[ C_{\rm rad}(p,\gamma) =\left[1+\left(\gamma-1+\frac2p\right)^2\right]^{-p/2}. \] For general, not necessarily radial, potentials, we identify explicit parameter regions where this constant remains sharp and establish two sufficient criteria for symmetry breaking. The exact transition remains open for $p\ne2$. In the quadratic case, we recover the known sharp constant and derive a decomposition of its deficit. At the critical exponent, we obtain an exact remainder identity for the logarithmic Hardy inequality, whose classical constant remains sharp among radial potentials. The logarithmic inequality fails at $p=1$.
item.dc:creator: Yerkin Shaimerdenov, Nurgissa Yessirkegenov

item.title: Sharp Thresholds of Instability for the Biharmonic Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the time-dependent biharmonic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with and without a mixed dispersion. We find the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence for the biharmonic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations without a mixed dispersion by establishing the modified cross-constraint variational method. Building on this work, we prove that the standing waves are strongly unstable without further assumptions on the frequency. The main new ingredients of which require us to provide a comparison of two variational problems, improved the method in Zhang [Comm PDEs, 2005, 30: 1429-1443]. In the latter part of the paper, we study the biharmonic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with a mixed dispersion, which destroys the scaling invariance. The single variational approach is utilized to obtain the sharp threshold of blow-up and global existence, and strong instability of standing waves.
item.dc:creator: Shanshan Fu, Shihui Zhu

item.title: Nonradial entire solutions of the critical H\'enon equation for every $\alpha>2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the critical H\'enon equation $-\Delta u=|x|^{\alpha}u^{(N+2+2\alpha)/(N-2)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$. Gladiali, Grossi, and Neves (\emph{Advances in Mathematics}, 2013) constructed nonradial continua bifurcating at $\alpha_k=2(k-1)$, $k\ge2$, and conjectured that these continua are confined to the even parameters. Jiang and Xiong (2026) disproved this conjecture by obtaining nonradial solutions in punctured neighborhoods of $\alpha_k$ for even $k>(N-2)/2$. We prove that positive nonradial finite-energy entire solutions exist for every $\alpha>2$ in every dimension $N\ge3$. The proof introduces a global variational construction by direct minimization on a monotonicity cone on the Emden--Fowler cylinder.
