Angular and axial order restore compactness in every finite $L^r$, $r>2$, despite Sobolev supercriticality, and invariance of the linear resolvent yields the full equation. This constructs a solution at each prescribed parameter without continuing local bifurcation branches. The solutions have Newtonian decay, are invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and the Kelvin transform, and have energy strictly below the radial level. We also obtain a second solution for every $\alpha>6$ in even dimensions, nonvertical branches at every $\alpha_k$ with $k\ge2$ even without dimension restrictions, a cubic energy law, and rigidity near $\alpha=0$ under bounded cylindrical amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Le

item.title: The polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.02448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive classical solutions of the polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden system $(-\Delta)^m u=|x|^\alpha v^p$, $(-\Delta)^m v=|x|^\beta u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $m\ge2$, $p,q\ge1$, $pq>1$, and $\alpha,\beta\ge0$. We prove that there is no such solution whenever $\frac{n+\alpha}{p+1}+\frac{n+\beta}{q+1}>n-2m$, in every dimension and without any assumption on the behavior of the solutions at infinity. Combined with an existence result of Villavert, this proves the polyharmonic H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjecture of Phan for $m\ge2$: for these exponents and weights, a positive classical solution exists if and only if $\frac{n+\alpha}{p+1}+\frac{n+\beta}{q+1}\le n-2m$. The proof has two parts. We first show that positivity forces $(-\Delta)^i u>0$ and $(-\Delta)^i v>0$ for $1\le i\le m-1$. For $m$ even this needs $pq>1$, and explicit radial examples show that it fails when $pq<1$ and when $p=q=1$. The system is then equivalent to a weighted integral system with a Riesz kernel of order $2m$. For such integral systems we prove the corresponding Liouville theorem for every Riesz order $\mu\in(1,n)$, adapting a recent argument for the second-order case that combines a localized virial identity with an interval comparison along source layers.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Le

item.title: Validity of three-dimensional axisymmetric steady Prandtl expansion
item.description: arXiv:2611.02492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study steady axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flows with swirl in the circular cylinder $\mathcal C_L=(0,L)\times B_2(0,1)$ with the no-slip condition on the stationary lateral wall. For the leading Euler velocity $(u_e^0,w_e^0,\theta_e^0)=(1,0,r K(r))$, where $K(r)=H(r^2)$ is a prescribed smooth radial function, we construct and justify a Prandtl expansion as $\varepsilon \to 0$ for sufficiently small fixed $L$. The expansion accounts for both axial and azimuthal boundary layers, including the case of a Blasius leading axial profile with nonzero swirl. Weighted estimates at the symmetry axis and coupled remainder estimates yield a uniform velocity error bound.
item.dc:creator: Yan Guo, Hailiang Li, Xiangyu Ma, Mingyue Zhang

item.title: Radial and nonradial solutions for nonlinear scalar field equations and a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.02524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A nonlinear scalar field equation is studied, which takes the form \begin{equation*} - \triangle{u}=g(u) \ \textrm{in} \ R^{N}, \quad \quad u \in E, \end{equation*} where $E$ is a suitable Banach space.. The nonlinear term $g(s)$ has subcritical growth at infinity. Near $s=0$, the nonlinear term $g(s)$ grows like $s^q$ for any $q>0$ if $N=2$ and for any $q \in (0,\ (N+2)/(N-2))$ if $N\ge 3$. Through the technique of adding one dimension of space, by mountain pass theorem and symmetric mountain theorem, we prove the multiplicity of radial solutions if $N\ge 2$ and the multiplicity of nonradial solutions if $N\ge 4$. Unlike [1] and [2], the proof presented here does not rely on any decomposition results. During the treatment for $N=2$, we provide a new proof for certain Gagliardo-Nirenberg type inequality on $R^2$, which is originally due to [3]. Based on this inequality we get a Trudinger-Moser type inequality involving gradient norm through Taylor expansion. Eventually we construct a special path to obtain the least energy level for solutions. [1] J. Mederski, Nonradial solutions of nonlinear scalar field equations. Nonlinearity 33 (2020), 6349--6380. [2] L. Jeanjean, S.S. Lu, Nonlinear scalar field equations with general nonlinearity. Nonlinear Anal. 190 (2020), 111604. [3] D.E. Edmunds, A.A.Ilyin, Asymptotically sharp multiplicative inequalities. Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995) 71--74.
item.dc:creator: Qiuping Lu, Shuolei Liu

item.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations by One Noise Component
item.description: arXiv:2611.02557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus with multiplicative It\^o noise which is driven by a single Brownian motion and acts only through the vertical velocity component. Such a noise is strongly degenerate: An infinite-dimensional part of the velocity field is not forced at all. We show that it nevertheless has a regularizing effect. For a linear noise, strong solutions whose initial data have no unforced part are global with probability tending to one as the noise intensity grows. For a suitable nonlinear noise, the same holds for arbitrary $\mathrm{H}^1$ data, together with smallness of the space-time $\mathrm{L}^6$-norm of the vertical velocity. As a deterministic counterpart, we give a self-contained proof that a quintic damping of the vertical component yields global regularity, and the same argument shows that, under the linear noise, blow-up can only occur if the vertical velocity leaves $\mathrm{L}^6_{t,x}$.
item.dc:creator: Felix Brandt, Igor Kukavica

item.title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.02570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.
item.dc:creator: Qixing Ding, Jia-Cheng Zhao

item.title: The dual Orlicz-Minkowski problem for capillary hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $\phi(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+h\nu$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Ya Gao

item.title: Weighted Sobolev regularity and failure of profile convergence associated with the scattering operator for the three-dimensional cubic Klein-Gordon equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scattering problem for the three-dimensional nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation \begin{align*} u_{tt}-\Delta u+u=\pm u^3 \end{align*} is studied. It was shown that the scattering operator $\mathbf{S}$ for the equation is well-defined on a neighborhood of 0 in the Sobolev space $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}:=H^{1/2}(\mathbb{R}^3) \oplus H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, and that if $\Phi_-$ is sufficiently small in $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}$ and belongs to $\mathcal{S} \oplus \mathcal{S}$, then $\mathbf{S}\Phi_-$ is also in $\mathcal{S} \oplus \mathcal{S}$, where $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is the Schwartz space. In the present paper, however, we prove that for any non-zero real-valued $\Phi_-\in\mathcal{S}\oplus\mathcal{S}$ whose $\mathcal{H}^{1/2}$-norm is sufficiently small, the corresponding solution $u$ satisfies \[ U(-t) \,{}^t(u(t),\partial_t u(t)) \not\to \mathbf{S}\Phi_- \quad(t\to+\infty) \] in the weighted Sobolev space $H^{1,3}(\mathbb{R}^3)\oplus H^{0,3}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ although $U(-t)\,{}^t(u(t),\partial_t u(t))$ converges to $\mathbf{S}\Phi_-$ in $H^{1,\sigma}(\mathbb{R}^3)\oplus H^{0,\sigma}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for any $\sigma<3$. Here, $U(t)$ denotes the free Klein-Gordon evolution group.
item.dc:creator: Hironobu Sasaki

item.title: Capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.02732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$, we study the long-time existence and asymptotic behavior of an even normalized capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$. When $pq\geq0$, the flow exists for all positive time and the evolving hypersurfaces converge smoothly along a sequence of times tending to infinity to a stationary solution of the normalized problem. If $p\neq q$, a dilation of the limit solves the unnormalized problem.
item.dc:creator: Jinrong Hu, Yingxiang Hu, Bo Yang

item.title: Quasiconvexity and Lower Semicontinuity in the Riemannian Setting
item.description: arXiv:2611.02792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a notion of quasiconvexity for integrands defined on the bundle of linear maps between the tangent spaces of two smooth, connected and complete Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ and $(N,h)$, naturally extending the classical Euclidean notion. For continuous integrands, we prove that this Riemannian quasiconvexity is equivalent to the sequential lower semicontinuity of the associated functional $$ F(u,\Omega)=\int_\Omega f(du)\,d\mu_g $$ with respect to the weak$^*$ convergence in $W^{1,\infty}(\Omega,N)$, in the intrinsic sense adopted in the paper, for every bounded open subset $\Omega\subseteq M$. We then establish the Riemannian analogues of the Acerbi--Fusco theorems for Carath\'eodory integrands satisfying the corresponding growth conditions, for every $1\leqslant p\leqslant+\infty$, with respect to the weak and weak$^*$ notions of convergence considered here.
item.dc:creator: Aurora Corbisiero, Chiara Leone, Carlo Mantegazza

item.title: The anelastic approximation and convergence rate for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with ill-prepared data in bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.02831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We justify the anelastic approximation and establish a convergence rate for local strong solutions to the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with ill-prepared initial data and vorticity-slip boundary conditions. When the Mach and Froude numbers vanish at the same rate $\epsilon$, the system converges to an anelastic system with nonconstant hydrostatic density. Compared with the incompressible limit, the balance between singular pressure and gravity generates a variable-coefficient acoustic operator and additional commutators. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce the pressure perturbation adapted to the hydrostatic balance and establish weighted acoustic and vorticity estimates, yielding uniform-in-$\epsilon$ estimates. We then use the weighted Helmholtz decomposition and time-averaging technique to prove the strong convergence of solenoidal component of the momentum and obtain an error bound controlled by $\epsilon$ and the initial error in the projected momentum. Our analysis reveals the weighted cancellation mechanism that applies to singular limits around a class of nonconstant equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Yaobin Ou, Ping Wang

item.title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.02864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.
item.dc:creator: Adel Blouza, Siyu Cen, Yavar Kian

item.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: Uniqueness and shape of simplex ground states for aggregation--diffusion energies with mild repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2611.02890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^d$ of the free energy $\mathcal{E}_\kappa=\mathcal{W}+\kappa\mathcal{U}$, where $\mathcal{W}$ is a power-law interaction energy with mild repulsion and $\mathcal{U}$ is the porous-medium internal energy with exponent $m>1$. In a range of exponents that we call the strict simplex regime, results of Lim--McCann and Davies--Lim--McCann show that $\mathcal{W}$ is minimized, uniquely up to rigid motions, by equal point masses at the vertices of a regular unit $d$-simplex. Diffusion excludes such atomic minimizers for every $\kappa>0$. We prove that uniqueness nevertheless persists: for every fixed $m>1$ and all sufficiently small $\kappa>0$, the free energy has a unique global minimizer up to rigid motions. After a suitable rigid motion, this minimizer is invariant under every symmetry of the simplex, and its support splits into $d+1$ clusters near the vertices, each of mass exactly $1/(d+1)$; in particular, it is not radially symmetric when $d\geq2$. The clusters have width of order $\kappa^{1/(d(m-1)+2)}$, which is also the exact order of the quadratic Wasserstein distance from the minimizer to the atomic simplex measure. Rescaled at this scale, the clusters converge in $L^1$ and $L^\infty$ to explicit Barenblatt-type profiles supported on ellipsoids determined by the Hessian of the simplex potential. For $d\geq2$ these ellipsoids are spheroids flattened along the directions of the vertices; when the repulsive exponent exceeds two, their aspect ratio equals $(d+1)^{-1/2}$, independently of all other parameters. At the endpoint $(4,2)$ of this regime in dimensions $d\geq2$, where the zero-diffusion minimizer is not unique, we show instead that vanishing diffusion selects the uniform spherical shell.
item.dc:creator: Tongseok Lim, Geuntaek Seo

item.title: Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fisher-KPP equations on hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate or in the distance from a point or a geodesic. We determine spectral thresholds for extinction and persistence, including critical extinction from $L^2$ data, and characterize the signed speeds of horospherical fronts. In the hyperbolic plane, we construct a smooth periodic reaction admitting a positive stationary solution that decays away from a geodesic, and determine the spreading speed along the geodesic. For constant linear growth, we obtain logarithmic level positions with bounded error for balls, horoballs and geodesic tubes.
item.dc:creator: Yuanyang Hu

item.title: On blow-up for the cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.02970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth, strictly positive solutions of the three-dimensional cut-off Boltzmann equation with very hard potentials whose densities become unbounded in finite time. A main ingredient is a new velocity weight that is Gaussian on a ball and has a polynomial tail of fixed order. We establish coercive estimates for the linearized collision operator and bilinear estimates for the collision term, with constants independent of the radius of the Gaussian region. Combining these weighted estimates with an imploding solution of the compressible Euler equations, we develop an energy framework that controls the Boltzmann solution up to the blow-up time. The initial data agree with a constant Maxwellian outside a bounded spatial region and have finite relative entropy.
item.dc:creator: Ning Jiang, Feng Shao, Dongyi Wei, Zhifei Zhang, Kai Zhou

item.title: Symmetry, uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions of the Choquard equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive solutions \(Q\in H^1(\mathbb R^N)\) of \[-\Delta Q+Q=(I_\alpha*Q^p)Q^{p-1},\] where \(I_\alpha\) is the Riesz potential of order \(\alpha\), \(N\ge1\), \(0<\alpha<N\), \(p>1+\alpha/N\), and \((N-2)p<N+\alpha\). We prove that every such solution is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing about some point. For \(p\ge2\), we establish uniqueness up to translations and show that the real linearized operator has Morse index one and kernel spanned by \(\partial_1Q,\ldots,\partial_NQ\). The symmetry proof uses the method of moving planes. Uniqueness follows from nondegeneracy and compactness through a continuation argument.
item.dc:creator: Song Fan, Gui-Dong Li, Jianjun Zhang

item.title: Stochastic Homogenization of Schr\"odinger Equations with Exponentially Mixing Sub-Gaussian Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.03014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stochastic Schr\"odinger equation $ i\partial_t u_{\varepsilon} = H_{\varepsilon} u_{\varepsilon} $ with $ H_{\varepsilon} = -\Delta + V(x/\varepsilon) $, where V is a stationary ergodic sub-Gaussian field with exponential mixing. We establish the optimal algebraic error rate $ \varepsilon^{d/2} $ in $ L^2(\Omega; L^2_x) $ for every $ d\ge1 $, prove it sharp by a matching lower bound when $ \widehat{R}(0)>0 $, and upgrade the convergence of Zhang--Bal from convergence in probability to almost sure convergence. We further establish a Gaussian fluctuation central limit theorem with explicit covariance. The limiting fluctuation satisfies $ i\partial_t \mathcal{G} = (-\Delta + \bar{V})\mathcal{G} + \sqrt{\widehat R(0)}\,\dot W(t,x) $, a linear random Schr\"odinger equation driven by additive space-time white noise, where $ \bar{V} = \mathbb{E}[V] $ is the effective potential.
item.dc:creator: Fanfei Meng

item.title: On Higher Order Elliptic Differential Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.03037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we examine the positive preserving properties, or the lack thereof, for Green's operators of elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds. We will obtain the existence of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds whose lowest eigenvalue is not simple, and the existence of a large family of elliptic differential operators on closed manifolds that only have signed eigenfunctions associated with the lowest eigenvalue. That is, we will see that there is both "good news" and "bad news" when one studies the positivity preserving properties of Green's operators associated with higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds and the eigenproblem for higher order elliptic differential operators on smooth, closed Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: David Raske

item.title: Perturbation Analysis of Gravitational Collapse of Gaseous Stars in the Pressureless Euler-Poisson System
item.description: arXiv:2611.03061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The compressible Euler-Poisson system describes the full evolutionary processes of inviscid compressible gases, including compression, expansion, fluid motion, equilibrium states and gravitational collapse, under the combined effects of self-gravitation, pressure and inertial forces. It constitutes the fundamental macroscopic mathematical model for describing stellar structures, nebular evolution and gravitational collapse of gaseous celestial bodies. The system comprises mass conservation, momentum conservation, energy conservation laws coupled with the Poisson equation. Following the research in \cite{huang2022}, this paper investigates the quantitative relations among the relative perturbation amplitude of initial velocity, critical time and collapse time for gaseous stars undergoing gravitational collapse within the framework of the pressureless Euler-Poisson system. The closed-form formulas are verified against direct numerical integration, the accuracy of the asymptotic power law is quantified, and the relation between the two time scales is examined.
item.dc:creator: Xingchen Wang, Xiaomin Zhang

item.title: Singular evolution of Gaussian measures under energy-critical and supercritical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a family of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with odd-power nonlinearities and fractional dispersion in an energy-critical/supercritical regime. For a family of Gaussian measures supported on high-regularity spaces, we show that the flow immediately evolves these measures to ones that are mutually singular with respect to their initial distributions. In the cubic case, the threshold for singularity exactly corresponds to the energy scaling for the equation. In particular, we establish singular evolution of Gaussian measures under the flow of the energy-critical cubic NLS on the 4-dimensional torus.
item.dc:creator: James Coe

item.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: $C^1$-estimates in nonlocal parabolic problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under a minimal tail condition, local weak solutions to a class of nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations modeled on the fractional heat equation possess continuous spatial derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Verena B\"{o}gelein, Naian Liao, Calvin Stanko

item.title: Global attractor for weakly damped nonlinear parametric Klein-Gordon Schr{\"o}dinger system
item.description: arXiv:2611.03129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a damped forced nonlinear Klein-Gordon Schr\''{o}dinger (KGS) system known as the parametric KGS system with Yukawa coupling. We prove the regularity of the global attractor for this infinite-dimensional dynamical system, i.e. that the global attractor is included into a smaller Sobolev space than the energy space. We prove that this global attractor has finite fractal dimension, without any assumption on the decay of the forcing terms.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series S, 2026, 26, pp.288-302
item.dc:creator: Olivier Goubet (Paradyse, LPP), Marilena Poulou

item.title: Global attractor for two-dimensional weakly damped nonlinear parametric Klein-Gordon Schrodinger system
item.description: arXiv:2611.03134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a damped forced nonlinear Klein-Gordon Schr {\"o}dinger (KGS) system known as the parametric KGS system with Yukawa coupling where the space variable belongs to R 2 . We prove the existence of a global attractor in dimension 2. Moreover we prove that this global attractor is regular and has finite fractal dimension.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Goubet (Paradyse, LPP), Marilena Poulou

item.title: Global Well-posedness of Incompressible MHD System with Density-dependent Viscosity in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.03182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible Magnetohydrodynamic equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum. For initial data with positive mass, finite second moment of density, and zero total momentum, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions when the viscosity is sufficiently close to one in $L^\infty$. The smallness threshold may depend on the initial data, while no separate smallness condition is imposed on the initial velocity or magnetic field. We obtain uniform-in-time bounds for the density second moment and its $H^1\cap W^{1,q}$ norm, where $q>2$. Moreover, for every $\eta\in(0,1)$, $\|\sqrt{\rho}u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}+\|b(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}$ decays at the rate $t^{-\eta/2}$, and the $H^1$ norms of $\nabla u$, $P$, and $\nabla b$ decay at the rate $t^{-(1+\eta)/2}$. The proof combines a velocity decomposition based on Hardy-space estimates with magnetic-field integrability and time-weighted energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xue Wang

item.title: A Note on Fractional Sobolev inequalities revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.03185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we extend the analysis of homogeneous fractional Sobolev inequalities in the paper by A.D. Nguyen, J. I. D{\i}az, and Q.-H. Nguyen (2020). We combine their subcritical proof with the first author's adaptation to the supercritical case to provide a short interpolation-based proof for the critical case.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Leoni, Asher Wheaton

item.title: Neumann problem for Hessian equation and geometric inequalities in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.03206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the existence of solutions to the Neumann problem for the Hessian equation on a smooth, bounded strictly static convex domain in hyperbolic space. The boundary condition determines a unique compatibility constant, and admissible solutions are unique up to a multiple of the static potential. As an application, we give a direct analytic proof of some weighted geometric inequalities for the static convex domain in hyperbolic space.
item.dc:creator: Liangjun Weng

item.title: The Dirichlet problem for quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere equations on flat quaternionic quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.03214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove smooth solvability of the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere equations on smooth relatively compact domains in ${\mathbb H}^m/\Gamma$, where $m\ge2$ and $\Gamma$ is a discrete additive subgroup: for a smooth positive density, the existence of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution guarantees the existence and uniqueness of the smooth admissible solution. The technique of the proof is a simple adaptation from the Ph.D. Thesis of Jingyong Zhu [25] in 2017, supervised by Xinan Ma, which is a joint work of Ma and Zhu. The claim [22, Theorem A.1] by OpenAI on Sogge's local smoothing conjecture is a special case of our theorem.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Nan Ma, Jingyong Zhu

item.title: Global Stability and Decay for the 2D Anisotropic Navier-Stokes Equations with Fractional Horizontal Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although the classical Yudovich theory guarantees global existence and uniqueness of two-dimensional Euler solutions with bounded vorticity, their higher-order norms may still grow in time. This raises a fundamental question: how much dissipation we need to ensure global stability and decay? While the full Laplacian dissipation is sufficient, the stabilizing effect of weaker, anisotropic dissipation is considerably more subtle. In this paper, we investigate the global stability and long-time decay of the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation $\Lambda_1^{2s}u$, where $s<1$. A central challenge is to recover sufficient decay of the second velocity component, whose weak dissipation obstruct the closure of conventional anisotropic energy estimates. Previous work by Wang-Wu-Zhu [arXiv:2601.16110] resolved this difficulty whereas the spatial weighted energy functionals must be used when $s$ approaches $1$. The main purpose of our manuscript is to remove this restriction. We introduce a hierarchy of carefully designed time-weighted anisotropic energy functionals which captures the interplay between horizontal fractional dissipation and the decay of velocity components. Under such initial assumptions, the characteristics of anisotropic dissipation is presented more straightforwardly, which also reveals the more essential intrinsic structure of fluid stability.
item.dc:creator: Chenyan Shen, Dan Wu, Yi Zhu

item.title: Persistence of $C^2$ regularity for aggregation patches
item.description: arXiv:2611.03258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove persistence of $C^2$ boundary regularity for patch solutions of the two-dimensional aggregation transport equation, in contrast with the known $C^2$ ill-posedness of Euler vortex patches. More generally, we consider transport equations with kernels of the form $L(\nabla N)$, where $N$ is the fundamental solution of the Laplacian and $L$ is a linear map. We show that $C^2$ regularity persists for every $C^2$ initial patch if and only if $L$ is a scalar multiple of the identity. Our approach builds on the curvature formulation introduced by Kiselev and Luo.
item.dc:creator: Juan Carlos Cantero, Marc Maga\~na

item.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.03278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log \rho(g,t)$ as $\rho \rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -\Delta_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenb\"ock spectral gap boost $\lambda_1(-\Delta_{SE(3)}) \ge \lambda_1(-\Delta_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincar\'e coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.
item.dc:creator: Pilhwa Lee

item.title: Selection principle for Weak KAM solutions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ via large deviation principle for diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equations generally admit many weak KAM solutions. The question is how to select one weak KAM solution that reflects a meaningful physical principle. In this paper, we propose a selection principle for Hamilton-Jacobi equations arising from the large deviation principle of general drift-diffusion processes on $\mathbb{R}^n$ based on the exponential asymptotics of invariant measures. We first characterize the Aubry set as the finitely many equilibria of the drift, using an action estimate from the orthogonal decomposition of the drift. For any boundary data on the Aubry set compatible with the Peierls barrier, we construct the unique coercive weak KAM solution with these boundary data, which is also the maximal locally Lipschitz viscosity solution. The Freidlin-Wentzell graph formula then provides the boundary data on the Aubry set that select the unique weak KAM solution. The selected solution is exactly the rate function in the large deviation principle for invariant measures in the zero noise limit. We also show that this rate function is the vanishing viscosity limit, to which the viscous approximations converge locally uniformly. Finally, under additional regularity assumptions, we show that the long-time and zero-noise limits commute for suitably prepared initial densities.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Gao, Yuxi Han

item.title: Radial Symmetry and Nondegeneracy for Singular Liouville Systems with Small Singular Exponents
item.description: arXiv:2611.03456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the classification (Lin and Zhang, Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e Anal. Non Lin\'eaire \textbf{27}, 2010) to finite-mass singular Liouville systems with sufficiently small positive singular exponents. For symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, irreducible and invertible coupling matrices, every solution whose mass vector lies near a fixed compact subset of the regular mass surface is radial about the singular point and is uniquely determined by its component masses up to dilation. We also establish nondegeneracy modulo dilation. To overcome the failure of the moving-plane argument for positive exponents, we use compactness and a local reduction based on integral identities. The results also hold for nonzero nonnegative exponent vectors and for small mixed-sign vectors satisfying an explicit integral inequality.
item.dc:creator: Zetao Cheng, Haoyu Li, Lei Zhang

item.title: Sharp bounds and asymptotic profiles for Lane-Emden systems at the Serrin threshold
item.description: arXiv:2611.03483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify isolated singularities of $p$-Laplace and $k$-Hessian Lane--Emden systems on their Serrin critical curves without radial symmetry. Our approach reconstructs a radial profile from the source measures through a truncated Wolff potential, providing a nonlinear counterpart of spherical averaging. For upper inequalities at equal powers, we determine the sharp joint logarithmic lower bound on the zero-mass singular branch. A radial pair attains this bound while both normalized components oscillate between zero and infinity. For exact systems at equal powers, we obtain a common second-order profile with a shared phase and a sharp two-term logarithmic expansion of the component difference. At unequal powers, we establish power--logarithmic asymptotics with explicit leading constants. These asymptotics hold uniformly in direction.
item.dc:creator: Shiguang Ma, Shengyang Zang

item.title: Gradient flow formulation and discrete approximation of reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.03491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize a class of possibly degenerate nonlinear reaction-cross-diffusion systems with size exclusion as (non-metric) gradient flows in continuity-equation format driven by entropy. We then establish a connection between these systems and discrete reaction networks by proving an EDP-type lower limit inequality for the associated gradient systems. In the non-degenerate case, we show a chain rule identity that allows us to identify minimizers of the corresponding energy-dissipation functional as weak solutions to the PDE system. In conjunction with the lower limit, this yields an alternative proof of existence of weak solutions and their approximability by solutions to the proposed discrete ODE systems. Finally, we generalize our results to models including drift terms by extending the established framework to tilted energy landscapes.
item.dc:creator: Georg Heinze

item.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schr\"odinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
item.dc:creator: Yinghao Gong

item.title: Construction of the 2D non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure via stochastic quantisation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide the first mathematical construction of the non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure on a two-dimensional torus by implementing Parisi and Wu's ``stochastic quantisation'' procedure. We use a specific gauge covariant (but non-Markovian) approximation to the previously constructed associated Langevin dynamics and develop a covariant paracontrolled calculus for it. This allows us to obtain short-time control over times that are much longer than what the cubic nonlinearity na\"ively suggests. When combined with the decay properties of the Yang-Mills-Higgs action under the deterministic gradient flow, as well as a quantitative measure of how the noise pushes the dynamic away from Yang-Mills connections, this is good enough to yield uniform-in-time bounds. We finally show that there exists a renormalisation under which our gauge covariant approximation converges to the Langevin dynamics (modulo gauge transformation) and that the latter is topologically irreducible and strong Feller. It therefore admits a unique invariant measure, providing the sought-after construction. Our construction is non-perturbative and works in particular for any fixed values of the coupling constants.
item.dc:creator: Bjoern Bringmann, Sky Cao, Martin Hairer, Wenhao Zhao

item.title: A hyperbolic nonlinear Schr\"odinger system in multiple spatial dimensions: structure, convergence, and numerical discretization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and study a first-order hyperbolic approximation of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in $N$ spatial dimensions. This is an extension of the recently-proposed 1D hyperbolic NLS model. We study the structure and properties of the hyperbolic approximation and their relation to those of the original system. We show that the N-dimensional hyperbolic system exactly conserves analogs of the mass, energy, and momentum, and that it possesses stationary solutions that are closely related to those of NLS. The hyperbolic system is also shown to admit plane-wave solutions that share some stability properties with those of NLS, and that relaxation can shrink the focusing low-wavenumber modulational instability band as well as introduce a high-wavenumber instability band not present in NLS. We also show that solutions of the hyperbolic system converge to solutions of NLS in the relaxation limit. We present an adaptive-mesh finite volume discretization of the hyperbolic system and demonstrate its effectiveness in handling simulations, including those with geometric obstacles or non-periodic boundary conditions. The effectiveness of the numerical scheme is demonstrated through examples including a Bose-Einstein condensate, line soliton instability, and superflow past a cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Mu\~noz-Moncayo, Abhijit Biswas, David I. Ketcheson, Manvendra Rajvanshi

item.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.00139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Wa\.zewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Dain Kim, Tristan Ozuch

item.title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.00598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=\lambda\Psi_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(\Psi_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(\lambda\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_\delta(\lambda+W/\lambda)\leq T\leq \lambda^{1+\kappa_d^{\rm BA}-\delta}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(\kappa_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(\lambda^3+\lambda W)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asymp\lambda^2\) between \(\lambda^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda WT}\). The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Fu

item.title: Spectral and convex geometry of $\alpha$-harmonic maps and sharp Morse index rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a weighted scalar spectral geometric description of Sacks-Uhlenbeck $\alpha$-harmonic maps into round spheres and identify its convex geometry realization for $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere. More precisely, we establish a one-to-one correspondence, modulo orientation preserving isometries of $\mathbb{S}^2$, between orientation preserving $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere and positive Codazzi tensors satisfying a determinant bound and a compatibility condition with the prescribed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$. These tensors are the radii tensors of auxiliary strictly convex surfaces, and the weighted scalar forms in spectral geometry equal $-\alpha$ times the second variations of the enclosed volumes with respect to the support functions. Using these spectral geometry and convex geometry results, we prove a sharp Morse index characterization of isometric equatorial parametrizations among $\alpha$-harmonic $2$-spheres in the round $n$-sphere. We also prove that every $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphism between unit round $2$-spheres is orthogonal for all $\alpha>1$. Equivalently, the only admissible positive Codazzi tensor whose reconstructed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has Gaussian curvature $1$ is $(\kappa+2)^{\alpha-1}\bar{g}$, where $\bar{g}$ is the unit round metric.
item.dc:creator: Rui Gao, Miaomiao Zhu

item.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates. The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution. We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.
item.dc:creator: Qi Yao

item.title: A structure-preserving finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility
item.description: arXiv:2611.00837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct and analyze a fully discrete finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility. The scheme combines a standard two-point flux approximation of diffusion, the L1 approximation of the Caputo derivative on a uniform time grid, and a semiconvex splitting of the potential, and it discretizes the inverse mobility by a secant average multiplying the entire L1 derivative. The key estimate is a lower bound for the accumulated pairing of this weighted L1 derivative with the solution increments in terms of the accumulated L1 quadratic form. Using this lower bound, we derive a discrete energy estimate and the time regularity required for compactness. For twice continuously differentiable semiconvex potentials satisfying sign conditions outside $(-1,1)$ and initial data in $H^1(\Omega)$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, we prove existence of at least one fully discrete solution on every admissible finite volume mesh and every uniform time grid. Every such solution satisfies the maximum bound principle and a discrete energy bound relative to the initial energy, without a time-step restriction. In up to three space dimensions, under a mesh regularity condition with a constant independent of the mesh size, we prove that any sequence of fully discrete solutions has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$ to a weak solution of the continuous problem as the mesh size and time step tend to zero. As a consequence, we obtain existence of a weak solution in one and two space dimensions, and in three dimensions whenever such meshes exist.
item.dc:creator: Yonghyeon Jeon, Kiwoong Kwon

item.title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
item.description: arXiv:2611.00932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ba\~nuelos, Adam Os\k{e}kowski

item.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.00975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $\mu_n \to \mu$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.
item.dc:creator: Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_\omega^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.
item.dc:creator: Jie Chen, Fan Gu, Xianliang Zhao

item.title: Bochner-Riesz means for Laguerre expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the $L^p$ norm convergence of Bochner-Riesz means $S_R^\delta f$, $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^+,d\mu_\beta)$ associated to Laguerre expansions of type $\beta \geq -1/2$. For any given $1 < p < \infty$ and $\beta > -1/2$, we provide a complete characterisation of the order $\delta$ for which these means are uniformly bounded on $L^p$ spaces. A particularly noteworthy phenomenon arises for $-1/3 <\beta <0$, where the admissible $(p, \delta)$ region differs substantially from those for $ -1/2 \leq \beta \leq -1/3$ or $\beta \geq 0$. Interestingly, the convergence for $-1/3 < \beta <0$ is an interaction between the ranges $ -1/2 \leq \beta \leq -1/3$ and $\beta \geq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Himani Sharma, Adam Sikora, Sundaram Thangavelu

item.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.01303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schr\"odinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, where $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
item.description: arXiv:2611.01419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Vel\'azquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.
item.dc:creator: Argam Ohanyan

item.title: Double Fibration Transforms: Geometry and Microlocal Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.01760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Double fibration transforms integrate functions over families of submanifolds. We survey the recovery of singularities by both classical normal operator methods and direct analytic methods. We also discuss support theorems, injectivity and applications to geodesic ray transforms, seismic inversion and minimal surface data.
item.dc:creator: Shubham R. Jathar, Jesse Railo

item.title: Nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a nonlinear adiabatic theorem for the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation with a time-dependent trapping potential $V(x,t)$. If either (i) $V(\cdot,t)$ is smooth, subquadratic in space and with uniformly bounded spatial derivatives of order $\geq 2$, or (ii) $V(\cdot,t)$ is a uniformly bounded perturbation of a fixed non-negative potential which is asymptotically $|x|^m, m\geq 2$, then the GP equation has a global solution, which remains uniformly close to the instantaneous minimizer of the time-independent GP functional, provided the initial condition is a ground state. In fact, we show that the existence of a solution of the GP equation is the real bottleneck: If existence is assumed, then adiabaticity holds under very minimal assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Sven Bachmann, Severin Schraven

item.title: The geometric case of the Erd\H{o}s Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
item.description: arXiv:2611.02454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed $q\in(0,1)$, can a set of positive Lebesgue measure avoid every translated and dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$? OpenAI's release of October 6, 2026 shows that it can, with a compact subset of $[0,1]$ whose measure is arbitrarily close to one. We give a detailed exposition of the proof, using only finite probability and basic measure theory. The proof removes a small open set intersecting every copy, obtained from a random construction: fair random choices, attached to the cells of nested grids, route each point down a finite tree, and at the leaf reached a further random choice removes the point with probability $p$. The removed set therefore has expected density $p$, however large the tree, while the branching gives each copy many independent chances to intersect it. Each chance depends on only part of the tree, so its outcome changes at only a controlled number of dilations, and a union bound over finitely many representative dilations then covers every dilation. We also relate the proof to the earlier random-cell arguments going back to Kolountzakis (Bull. London Math. Soc. 29 (1997), 415--424) and to recent work on two-fold sumsets (arXiv:2607.03584) and on Rajchman measures (arXiv:2609.04456), and we show how the method of conditional expectations makes the construction deterministic.
item.dc:creator: Alex Iosevich, Alexia Yavicoli

item.title: Supermodularity and robust optimization in elliptic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study distributionally robust optimization problems constrained by semilinear elliptic PDEs. Uncertain nonnegative loads enter the PDE through $m$ intensity parameters, and damage is measured by integrating a nondecreasing convex function of the solution. We prove that, for coercive operators satisfying a positivity-preserving lattice condition, a nondecreasing concave reaction $g$ makes the damage nondecreasing, convex, and supermodular in the load intensities. Under nonnegative loading and $g(0)=0$, concavity is also necessary for these properties to hold for all admissible operators and damage functions. For Wasserstein uncertainty sets based on a weighted $\ell_1$ distance and $N$ observations, we show that at most $m+1$ nested stress corners are needed per observation. These corners form a set of at most $N(m+1)$ points that does not depend on the Wasserstein radius and supports a worst-case distribution for every radius. We compute the exact robust value by checking $\lambda=0$ and at most $Nm$ positive breakpoints, and we construct a worst-case distribution that moves each observation to a chain corner and splits at most one observation between two adjacent corners. We apply the results to a convex remediation-planning problem with Monod biodegradation. Numerical experiments show that the method requires far fewer PDE solves than enumerating all corners. Finally, a counterexample shows that supermodularity can fail for the fractional $p$-Laplacian when $p>2$.
item.dc:creator: Debangana Mukherjee, Akash Ashirbad Panda

item.title: Local null controllability of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis system by a Neumann boundary control
item.description: arXiv:2611.02621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove local null controllability for a parabolic equation coupled to an elliptic equation on a bounded interval. The drift depends on the elliptic variable, and a single control acts through the Neumann condition at the left endpoint. For every positive control time and every locally Lipschitz drift function, sufficiently small initial data in $L^\infty$ can be driven to zero by an $L^\infty$ boundary control. To construct the control, we extend the linear equation to a larger interval using an even extension of the initial datum and an odd extension of the drift. A distributed $L^2$ control in the added interval then gives a boundary control on the original interval. A heat kernel estimate bounds the derivative trace needed for this construction. We obtain the nonlinear result by a set-valued fixed point argument.
item.dc:creator: Mohmedmunavvar Mubarak Bapu

item.title: A Reilly approach to weighted curvature integral inequalities in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a polarized weighted Reilly identity and an exact deficit decomposition for weighted curvature integrals $I_j=\int_\Sigma VE_j~\mathrm{d}\mu$ in hyperbolic space, where $V=\cosh r$ and $E_j$ is the normalized $j$th mean curvature. For compact domains with smooth connected boundary, these yield $I_k^2\geq I_{k-1}I_{k+1}$ under intrinsic sub-staticity at $k=1$ and static convexity with $\kappa\in\Gamma_k\cap\overline{\Gamma}_{k+1}$ for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, with equality precisely for geodesic balls. Under $h\geq0$ and $Vh-V_\nu g\geq0$, log-concavity and a Euclidean mixed-volume representation recover the centered-ball comparisons conjectured by Hu and Li \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{HuLi}, allowing the weight center to lie outside the domain. Equality in these comparisons holds precisely for balls centered at the weight center.
item.dc:creator: Shengguang Bi, Yingxiang Hu

item.title: Limiting properties of Hermitian-Einstein metrics under variation of the K\"ahler class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behaviour of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold, as the underlying K\"ahler metric varies and its K\"ahler class changes. In particular, if the bundle stops being stable at some point, the Hermitian-Einstein metrics blow up, and their rescaling can be used to construct a destabilizing subsheaf, following the argument of Uhlenbeck and Yau. Furthermore, we study the behaviour of Chern connections of these metrics, and show, that after passing to a subsequence, and applying suitable gauge transforms these connections converge, and identify the blow-up locus of their Uhlenbeck limit.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Klemyatin

item.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.03295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets. As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $\tau = \min\{\lambda,1-\lambda\}$ in the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}. Finally, in the same fashion as Krist\'aly and P\^irvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Miguel Machado, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos

item.title: Sublinear Power-Law Growth of Level Set Diameters in Heterogeneous F-KPP Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03332v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every $\alpha\in(1/4,1)$, we construct a heterogeneous medium $\xi$ such that the diameter of the level sets of the solution to the F-KPP equation is of order $t^\alpha$ along a sequence of times tending to infinity. This is a natural continuation of a series of recent works establishing logarithmic lower bounds as well as linear asymptotics for the diameters of the respective level sets in random and deterministic heterogeneous media. Both results assume $\sup\xi > 2\inf\xi$; we also show that the diameter can diverge in the critical regime $\sup\xi=2\inf\xi$. A key ingredient is an estimate for branching Brownian motion with fixed time horizon $t$ and branching rate $1$ on the negative half-line and $2+t^{-\eta}$ on the positive half-line. This estimate exhibits a saturation transition: for $\eta<1/2$ the polynomial and logarithmic corrections to the extremal position depend on $\eta$, whereas for $\eta\geq1/2$ the extremal position becomes independent of $\eta$, up to an additive constant.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Drewitz, Pascal Hanigk, Lisa Hartung

item.title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.03372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Christof, Malte A. Peter, Michael Ulbrich

item.title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.03519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. We apply the result in three settings: mixing for a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system where the scalar actively drives the velocity, mixing for a passive scalar advected by two-dimensional Navier-Stokes driven by smooth-in-time stochastic forcing, and a black-box proof that negative-regularity mixing implies enhanced dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Agresti, William Cooperman, Patrick Flynn

item.title: Flexibility of Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions under metric variation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the surjectivity of the differential of the Laplace-Beltrami operator with respect to the metric parameter. We use the obtained results to prove that every small deformation of a nonconstant eigenfunction can be realized with a small perturbation of the metric. As a consequence, we prove that every generic property of smooth functions which is invariant under multiplication by a nonzero scalar is generic for eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, extending a result by Uhlenbeck.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Agrachev, Nicola Da Ponte, Antonio Lerario, Matteo Testa

item.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:1406.7675v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
item.dc:creator: Khalil Chouk, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: Topological Anderson Insulators by homogenization theory
item.description: arXiv:2311.15678v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central property of (Chern) topological insulators is the presence of robust asymmetric transport along interfaces separating two-dimensional insulating materials in different topological phases. A Topological Anderson Insulator is an insulator whose topological phase is induced by spatial fluctuations. This paper proposes a mathematical model of perturbed Dirac equations and shows that for sufficiently large and highly oscillatory perturbations, the systems is in a different topological phase than the unperturbed model. In particular, a robust asymmetric transport indeed appears at an interface separating perturbed and unperturbed phases. The theoretical results are based on careful estimates of resolvent operators in the homogenization theory of Dirac equations and on the characterization of topological phases by the index of an appropriate Fredholm operator.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Bal, Thuyen Dang

item.title: Oscillatory free boundary problems in heterogeneous media
item.description: arXiv:2404.03060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a class of free boundary problems with oscillatory singularities within heterogeneous media. Our main result yields sharp regularity estimates along the free boundary, provided the power of the singularity varies in a Dini-continuous fashion below a certain threshold. We also reveal an interesting repelling estimate preventing the free boundary from touching the region where the singularity power oscillates above the threshold.
item.dc:creator: Dami\~ao J. Ara\'ujo, Ginaldo S. S\'a, Eduardo V. Teixeira, Jos\'e Miguel Urbano
