item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schr\"odinger equation with mixed dispersion and Sobolev critical growth
item.description: arXiv:2502.02049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates normalized solutions to a focusing biharmonic Schr\"odinger equation with mixed dispersion and combined nonlinearities involving a lower-power perturbation and a Sobolev critical term. Under a suitable smallness condition on the prescribed mass and in the range \(2<p<2+\frac{4}{N}\), we establish the existence of a local minimizer of the associated energy functional on \(S_r(c)\) and infinitely many pairs of radial normalized solutions by combining the truncation technique, the concentration-compactness principle and genus theory. In particular, our results extend those of Alves et al. (Anal. Appl., (2025), doi: 10.1142/S0219530525500447) by removing the additional assumptions imposed in their work. In the range \(2+\frac{8}{N}<p<4^*\), we prove the existence of bounded radial constrained Palais-Smale sequences at mountain pass levels below the critical Sobolev threshold for sufficiently large \(\mu\). We further show that their nonzero weak limits are radial weak solutions, with strong convergence in the derivative norms and in the critical Lebesgue norm. Moreover, under an additional condition \((N)\) ensuring the strict negativity of the limiting Lagrange multiplier, the weak limit preserves the prescribed \(L^2\)-mass, and the Palais-Smale sequence converges strongly in \(H^2(\mathbb R^N)\). These results extend the previous studies of Chang et al. (arXiv preprint, (2023), arXiv: 2305.00327v1) and Bonheure et al. (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., (2019), doi:10.1090/tran/7769).
item.dc:creator: Jianlun Liu, Hong-Rui Sun, Ziheng Zhang

item.title: Smoothing effect for third order operators with variable coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2503.08656v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we study the smoothing effect of some variable coefficient operators of the form $D_t-A$, where $A$ is a Weyl-quantized pseudo-differential operator of order $m=2,3$. The class under consideration includes, among others, KdV-type and ultrahyperbolic Schr\"odinger operators. We prove homogeneous and inhomogeneous smoothing estimates and use them to get well-posedness results for some NLIVPs with derivative nonlinearities. Finally, we investigate the so called non-trapping property of the bicharacteristic curves of the principal symbol of our operators.
item.dc:creator: Serena Federico, Davide Tramontana

item.title: On an Iterative Scheme for the Spinorial Yamabe Equation on Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2506.18546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a fixed-point framework for non-linear boundary value problems for first-order elliptic operators on vector bundles, with primary application to the spinorial Yamabe and Brezis--Nirenberg equations. We prove existence and uniqueness of an $H^1$-solution under a smallness condition that is homogeneous under amplitude and operator scaling. The associated iterative scheme converges geometrically in $L^q$ and $H^1$, and the solution depends continuously on the harmonic representative of the boundary datum. Through bootstrapping, we obtain interior $C^{1,\alpha}$-regularity and boundary smoothness under Shapiro--Lopatinski conditions. The method is extended to families of small domains via rescaling to a fixed reference domain.
item.dc:creator: Eric Tr\'ebuchon

item.title: Wave packet decompositions and sharp bilinear estimates for rough Hamiltonian flows
item.description: arXiv:2509.23551v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is to prove bilinear $L^p$ estimates for rough dispersive evolutions satisfying non-degeneracy and transversality assumptions. The estimates generalize the sharp Fourier extension estimates for the cone and the paraboloid. We obtain the sharp dependence on transversality and sharp up to endpoints $L^p$ range. To this end, we combine an axiomatic induction-on-scales with the construction of a wave packet parametrix for dispersive equations with $C^{1,1}$-coefficients by using the FBI transform.
item.dc:creator: Robert Schippa, Daniel Tataru

item.title: Derivation of the fourth-order DLSS equation with nonlinear mobility via chemical reactions
item.description: arXiv:2510.07149v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a derivation of the one-dimensional fourth-order DLSS equation based on an interpretation as a chemical reaction network. We consider the rate equation on the discretized circle for a process in which pairs of particles occupying the same site simultaneously jump to the two neighboring sites; the reverse process involves pairs of particles at adjacent sites simultaneously jumping back to the site located between them. Depending on the rates, in the vanishing-mesh-size limit we obtain either the classical DLSS equation or a variant with nonlinear mobility of power type. Via EDP convergence, we identify the limiting gradient structure to be driven by entropy with respect to a generalization of diffusive transport with nonlinear mobility. Interestingly, the DLSS equation with power-type mobility shares qualitative similarities with the fast diffusion and porous medium equation, since we find traveling wave solutions with algebraic tails or compactly supported polynomials, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Mielke, Andr\'e Schlichting, Artur Stephan

item.title: A family of nonlocal energies whose minimizers are supported on two intervals
item.description: arXiv:2510.11662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the one-dimensional interaction energy $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(W*\rho)(x)d\rho(x) + \int_{\mathbb{R}}U(x)d\rho(x)$ where the interaction potential $W(x)= -\frac{|x|^b}{b},\,1\le b \le 2$ and the external potential $U(x)=\frac{|x|^4}{4}$, and $\rho$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the real line. Our main result shows that the minimizer is supported on two intervals when $1<b<2$, showing in particular how the support of the minimizer transits from an interval (when $b=1$) to two points (when $b=2$) as $b$ increases. As a crucial part of the proof, we develop a new version of the iterated balayage algorithm, the original version of which was designed by Benko, Damelin, Dragnev and Kuijlaars for logarithmic potentials in one dimension. We expect the methodology in this paper can be generalized to study minimizers of interaction energies in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose support is possibly an annulus.
item.dc:creator: Steven B. Damelin, Ruiwen Shu

item.title: Linear decay of the beta-plane equation near Couette flow on the plane
item.description: arXiv:2511.00667v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove new time decay estimates for the linearized $\beta$-plane equation near the Couette flow on the plane that combine inviscid damping and the dispersion of Rossby waves. Specifically, we show that the profiles of the velocity field components (i.e. $u(t,x+ty,y)$) decay pointwise on any compact set with polynomial rates. While mixing dominates for streamwise frequencies that are $O(1)$, dispersive effects need to be extracted for low streamwise frequencies that appear along a critical ray in frequency space.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bedrossian, Patrick Flynn, Sameer Iyer

item.title: From Kinetic Nonequilibrium to Deviatoric Stress: An Operator Formulation of the First-Order Chapman--Enskog Transport Map
item.description: arXiv:2511.05514v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Chapman--Enskog procedure provides the classical asymptotic connection between kinetic nonequilibrium and macroscopic viscous stress. The present work isolates its first-order kinetic-to-stress step as an explicit operator composition. The construction separates the leading-order streaming source, the collisional kinetic response, and the deviatoric second-moment projection into a single transport map. Under explicit solvability, coercivity and bounded-inverse, regularity, and controlled-remainder assumptions, this map is well defined and bounded; hypocoercive estimates may additionally be used in closing the conditional remainder bound. In particular, a nonzero first-order deviatoric stress requires a nonzero first-order kinetic correction, although the converse is not asserted. The result is not a new derivation of the Navier--Stokes constitutive law or viscosity coefficient; its contribution is to make the kinetic-to-macroscopic transport map and its analytic conditions explicit. A BGK example recovers the classical Newtonian constitutive relation.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Barkman

item.title: Stabilization and control of the semilinear hinged plate equation
item.description: arXiv:2511.17468v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we prove semiglobal stabilization and exact controllability results for semilinear plate equations with hinged boundary conditions and analytic nonlinearity, when the damping or control acts on a region where the linear Schr\"odinger equation is observable. At the core of these results lies a new unique continuation property for the nonlinear plate equation, which significantly relaxes the geometric conditions required for such a property to hold. This property is obtained by combining recent results on propagation of analyticity in time and unique continuation for linear plate operators. More broadly, our approach exploits the linear observability of the plate equation to establish both stabilization and control results. First, we prove exponential decay of the nonlinear energy under a defocusing assumption on the nonlinearity. Second, under a weaker asymptotic assumption on the nonlinearity, we prove semiglobal exact control by analyzing control properties inside the compact attractor provided by the dynamics of the damped equation.
item.dc:creator: Crist\'obal Loyola

item.title: Derivation of a nonlinear, history-dependent tissue-level current law for an electropermeabilization model via homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2512.23007v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a phenomenological electropermeabilization model in a periodic medium representing biological tissue. Starting from a cell-level model describing the electric potential and the degree of poration, we perform dimensional analysis to identify a relevant scaling in terms of a small parameter $\varepsilon$ - the ratio between the cell and the tissue size. The electric potential satisfies electrostatic equations in the extra- and intracellular domains, while its jump across the cell membrane evolves according to a nonlinear law coupled with an ordinary differential equation for the poration degree. We prove the well-posedness of the microscopic problem, derive a priori estimates, obtain formal asymptotics, and rigorously justify the expansion by combining two-scale convergence with monotonicity arguments. The resulting macroscopic model exhibits memory effects and a nonlinear, time-dependent effective current. It captures the nontrivial evolution of effective conductivity, including a characteristic drop reflecting the capacitive behavior of the lipid bilayer, in agreement with experimental data. Numerical computations of the effective conductivity confirm that, although the intracellular and extracellular bulk conductivities are constant, tissue conductivity varies nonlinearly with electric field strength, showing a sigmoid trend.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Geb\"ack, Ioanna Motschan Ulander, Irina Pettersson

item.title: On the dimension drop for harmonic measure on uniformly non-flat Ahlfors-David regular boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2601.16167v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend earlier results of Azzam on the dimension drop of the harmonic measure for a domain $\Omega\subset \R^{n}$ with $n\geq 3$, with dimensional Ahlfors regular boundary $\partial\Omega$ of dimension $s$ with $n-1-\delta_0 \leq s\leq n-1$, that is uniformly non flat. Here $\delta_0$ is a small positive constant dependent on the parameters of the problem. Our novel construction relies on elementary geometric and potential theoretic considerations. We avoid the use of Riesz transforms and compactness arguments, and also give quantitative bounds on the $\delta_0$ parameter.
item.dc:creator: Aritro Pathak

item.title: Normalized solutions for a critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg equation: the effect of the weights on the coupling range
item.description: arXiv:2601.20513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study normalized solutions of $-\mathrm{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) = \lambda |x|^{-2a}u + \beta |x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u + |x|^{-b2^\sharp}|u|^{2^\sharp-2}u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx = \rho^2$, where $0 < a < \frac{N-2}{2}$, $a < b < a+1$, $2 < q < 2^\sharp$, and $2^\sharp$ is the critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg exponent. Let $q_c$ denote the mass-critical exponent. For $2 < q < q_c$ and small $\beta > 0$, we obtain two positive radial solutions: a local minimizer with negative energy and a solution of mountain-pass type. For $q_c \le q < 2^\sharp$, there is a number $\beta_0 \ge 0$, defined through the energy level below which compactness holds, such that a positive radial ground state exists for every $\beta > \beta_0$. In the mass-critical case $q = q_c$, this holds for $\beta_0 < \beta < \beta^*$, where $\beta^*$ is explicit, and for $\beta \ge \beta^*$ the ground state level is zero and is not attained. Our main result is a necessary and sufficient condition on $N$, $a$, $b$ and $q$ for $\beta_0 > 0$. The condition holds only when $a$ is close to $\frac{N-2}{2}$, and it fails in the formal unweighted limit $a = b = 0$. When $\beta_0 > 0$, the ground state level is not attained for $0 < \beta < \beta_0$, and every normalized solution has energy above the compactness level. When $\beta_0 = 0$, we describe the behavior of ground states as $\beta \to 0$. The proofs combine the Pohozaev constraint, sharp estimates for the extremals of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, and a blow-up analysis in Emden-Fowler variables.
item.dc:creator: Divya Goel, Asmita Rai

item.title: Dimension of the singular set in the parabolic obstacle problem
item.description: arXiv:2603.06352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the singular set in the parabolic obstacle problem for general obstacles $\varphi \in C^{2,1}$, with $\Delta \varphi < 0$. We prove that the singular set has parabolic Hausdorff dimension at most $n-1$. Prior to our result, this was only known when $\Delta \varphi \equiv -1$. Our approach combines a truncated parabolic frequency formula and monotonicity estimates with an iterative argument showing that the frequency is saturated for all values of the truncation parameter between $2$ and $3$.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Mart\'inez, Xavier Ros-Oton

item.title: An inverse source problem for a fully nonlinear elliptic equation
item.description: arXiv:2606.06431v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an inverse source problem for fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form \[ F(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } \Omega. \] The question is whether the source term can be recovered from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. In two dimensions, the first linearization does not immediately give uniqueness: it leaves a natural conformal ambiguity in the linearized coefficients. For homogeneous nonlinearities $F$ with injective differential $DF$, we show that this ambiguity has a precise meaning at the level of the equation itself, namely that the source is determined up to an explicit scalar factor. The main point of the paper is to show how this remaining factor can be removed. We use the second linearization to extract information which is invisible at first order, and combine it with an algebraic nondegeneracy condition on the nonlinearity. Under this condition, the residual ambiguity is forced to be trivial, and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map uniquely determines the source. The result applies, in particular, to homogeneous admissible Hessian equations of Monge--Amp\`ere type and related examples.
item.dc:creator: Ching-Lung Lin, Yi-Hsuan Lin, Jenn-Nan Wang

item.title: The partial data Calder\'on problem in dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2606.10247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider an inverse boundary value problem for the time-independent Schr\"odinger equation in dimension three. We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined near a boundary point uniquely determines the potential in a neighborhood of the boundary point in the interior. In particular, we show that the uniqueness question can be reduced to the injectivity of a weighted X-ray transform, which links inverse boundary value problems to integral geometry.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Uhlmann, Yiran Wang

item.title: A new perspective in linear Cauchy Elasticity: variational minimum principles for statics, dynamics, and heterogeneous materials
item.description: arXiv:2606.24782v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A variational minimum principle for linear elastodynamics of a possibly heterogeneous material without a stored energy function is developed. It involves a change of variables to dual fields, and results in a degenerate elliptic Euler-Lagrange system, even when the primal elastodynamics is hyperbolic. Uniqueness assertions for the dual dynamic and static problems and implications of the degenerate ellipticity are sketched. Some implications pertaining to heterogeneous materials and ones with indefinite elastic moduli are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Amit Acharya

item.title: The Calder\'on problem for near-Euclidean metrics
item.description: arXiv:2606.26540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we consider the anisotropic Calder\'on problem of determining the potential from boundary measurements of the time-independent Schr\"odinger equation on compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary. We prove a global uniqueness theorem for small perturbations of the Euclidean metric.
item.dc:creator: Gunther Uhlmann, Yiran Wang

item.title: Steady Euler flows with contact discontinuities in infinitely long nozzles with general upstream data
item.description: arXiv:2607.04804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate steady compressible Euler flows in two-dimensional infinitely long nozzles, where the piecewise smooth upstream data admit a contact discontinuity. Except for the subsonicity condition, no additional constraints are imposed on the data. We establish existence and uniqueness on the maximal interval of wall amplitudes containing the straight-nozzle configuration, and show that the contact discontinuity curve is of class $C^{2,\alpha}$. An Euler--Lagrange transformation reduces the problem to a scalar elliptic equation in divergence form on a fixed strip, with discontinuous coefficients and the contact discontinuity conditions incorporated into the weak formulation. We further investigate the downstream asymptotic behavior and show that the convergence rate of the flow matches that of the nozzle walls.
item.dc:creator: Jun Chen, Xuemei Deng, Xiaoguang You

item.title: Propagation dynamics of an acid-mediated invasion model with degenerate tumor diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2607.13944v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate traveling wave fronts for an acid-mediated tumor invasion model with density-dependent degenerate diffusion. The model is a partially diffusive PDE--ODE system of Gatenby--Gawlinski type, in which the tumor diffusion coefficient $D(U)$ is allowed to be a general decreasing function satisfying $D(1)=0$. This degeneracy causes the traveling wave equation for the tumor component to lose uniform ellipticity near the healthy state, and hence standard arguments for nondegenerate reaction diffusion systems are not directly applicable. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a nonlinear change of variables which removes the degeneracy from the highest-order term of the tumor equation. For each fixed admissible tumor profile, the acid profile is represented by a Green kernel, while the healthy-tissue profile is obtained from an explicit integral formula. The transformed tumor profile is then constructed as the stationary limit of a uniformly parabolic auxiliary problem. By combining comparison principles, local Schauder estimates, carefully chosen super- and sub-solutions, and the Schauder fixed-point theorem, we prove the existence of traveling wave fronts for every wave speed $\theta\ge 2\sqrt{rD(0)}$. The resulting wave connects the tumor-dominant state $(0,1,1)$ at $z=-\infty$ to the healthy state $(1,0,0)$ at $z=+\infty$. We further establish strict pointwise bounds, monotonicity of all wave components, and one-sided exponential asymptotic estimates in both the transformed variable and the original traveling-wave variable.
item.dc:creator: Xinyue Cao, Quentin Griette, Xiong Li, Yang Wang

item.title: On the diffusive-mean field limit of a kinetic weakly interacting particle system
item.description: arXiv:2607.15896v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the joint diffusive-mean field limit for a system of weakly interacting kinetic Langevin dynamics, extending the results of Delgadino, Gvalani and Pavliotis (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2021) to the hypoelliptic/hypocoercive case. We show that, in the absence of phase transitions, the two limits commute, and we calculate the covariance matrix of the limiting Brownian motion using the Green-Kubo/Kipnis-Varadhan formula. However, at low temperatures, and in the presence of phase transitions, the two limits may not commute. We demonstrate our findings by providing a detailed analysis of the diffusive-mean field limit for the $O(2)$ model in a magnetic field. Our analysis is based on the systematic use of recently developed hypocoercivity techniques, together with an appropriate linearization of the mean field McKean-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck partial differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Gastaldello, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Gabriel Stoltz, Urbain Vaes

item.title: Dimension-Free Lipschitz Bounds for Brenier Maps to Compact Log-Concave Targets
item.description:
arXiv:2608.15906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d\geq1$, $\Lambda>0$, and $ho\in\mathbb{R}$, let $\mu=\mathcal{N}(0,\Lambda^{-1}\mathrm{Id})$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, where $\mathrm{Id}$ is the identity matrix, and let $
u$ be a probability measure whose support is a convex body $K$ of diameter $D=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and whose density is proportional to $e^{-W}$, where $\mathrm{D}^{2}W\succeq-ho\mathrm{Id}$. We prove that the Brenier map $T$ from $\mu$ to $
u$ has Lipschitz constant $\operatorname{Lip}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Lambda/(2\pi)}\int_{-D/2}^{D/2}e^{ho t^{2}/2}\,\mathrm{d}t$, which is sharp in every fixed dimension. For log-concave targets, the optimal coefficient of $\sqrt{\Lambda}\,D$ is $1/\sqrt{2\pi}$. For sources with finite second moment and density proportional to $e^{-V}$ for which $x\mapsto rac12\langle Qx,xangle-V(x)$ is convex, where $Q$ is symmetric positive definite, and log-concave targets with compact support $K$, the Brenier potential $\Phi$ satisfies $\partial_{vv}\Phi\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\langle Qv,vangle}\,w_{K}(v)$ in the sense of distributions, where $w_{K}(v):=\sup_{y\in K}\langle y,vangle-\inf_{y\in K}\langle y,vangle$ is the width of $K$ along $v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $C_{1}<0.463$. This removes Kolesnikov's $\sqrt d$ loss. For log-concave sources with $\mathrm{D}^{2}V\preceq\Lambda\mathrm{Id}$ and the target $
u$, the Brenier map $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Lip}(T)^{2}\leq\Lambda\int_{0}^{D^{2}/4}e^{ho t}\,\mathrm{d}t$, so $\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ has the optimal exponential rate $1/8$ in $ho D^{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Maja Gwozdz

item.title: Cumulative angular cancellation in Maz'ya's endpoint inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2609.12755v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish domain criteria for critical homogeneous potential inequalities in the plane. Assuming signed plane cancellation, uniform absolute summability of frozen annular moments at each boundary centre implies the nonlinear endpoint estimate on arbitrary bounded open sets. For the Newton kernel and trace-free quadratic integrands, uniform boundedness of signed cumulative moments over all source centres and truncation radii is necessary and sufficient; testing all translates and dilates of one fixed radial unit-mass mollifier suffices. Tangent-cone cancellation on finitely cornered Dini domains follows as a geometric corollary. On one explicit strictly convex, non-Dini $C^1$ domain, the estimate holds for $2\xi_1\xi_2$ and fails for $\xi_1^2-\xi_2^2$ with $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$ divergence. A Laplacian-measure extension transfers density estimates to PDE inequalities on the Dini class and on strictly convex $C^1$ domains. We also classify quadratic cancellation on polygons. The signed necessary-and-sufficient criterion is restricted to quadratic integrands.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Strong Solutions and Long-Time Behavior for One-Dimensional Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Thermodynamically Compatible Pressure Laws
item.description: arXiv:2609.15317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated in part by non-ideal equations of state such as the van der Waals law, we study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant positive viscosity and heat conductivity and general thermodynamically compatible pressure and internal-energy functions. Assuming $e_\theta>0$, we obtain local $H^1(\mathbb R)$ strong solutions for initial data with positive specific volume and temperature, without sign conditions on the pressure derivatives. Near an equilibrium satisfying $p_v(\bar v,\bar\theta)<0$, sufficiently small $H^1(\mathbb R)$ perturbations generate global strong solutions with uniform thermodynamic bounds and time-integrable dissipation. For the full constitutive class, all first spatial derivatives decay in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ and the perturbation converges to zero in $L^p(\mathbb R)$ for every $2<p\le\infty$. We also identify a locally entropy-affine subclass of constitutive laws for which a Fourier--Duhamel argument establishes convergence to equilibrium in $H^1(\mathbb R)$. For more general thermodynamically compatible constitutive laws, we establish a conditional criterion for convergence in $H^1(\mathbb R)$, based on the space-time integrability of the nonlinear pressure remainder in entropy variables.
item.dc:creator: Qingsong Zhao, Boran Zhu

item.title: Uniqueness for the inverse Schr\"odinger problem in the plane with $L^p$ potentials, $p>1$
item.description: arXiv:2609.28046v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded smooth domain. We prove that the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-\Delta+V$ uniquely determines every complex-valued potential $V\in L^p(\Omega)$, $p>1$, provided that zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue. This extends the previously known range $p>4/3$ to all $p>1$. The proof uses Bukhgeim's quadratic-phase solutions and an average of Alessandrini's identity over the phase center. After separating the Neumann-series tails, we show that each remaining Born term tends to zero. The fixed-order estimates combine bounds for the absolute kernels with oscillatory cancellation and a duality argument for the product of the two Cauchy transforms.
item.dc:creator: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin I. C\^arstea, Jenn-Nan Wang

item.title: Local stability of direct Mach configurations
item.description: arXiv:2609.35365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the local stability of direct Mach configurations for the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations. Given a piecewise constant direct Mach configuration with subsonic flow behind both the reflected shock and the Mach stem, we prove that under a transversality condition on the shock polar loops and a suitable condition on the truncation segment, every sufficiently small perturbation of the incoming flow gives rise to a Mach configuration that is a small perturbation of the background one, in the sense that the reflected shock, the Mach stem and the slip line, together with the downstream subsonic flow, stay close to their background counterparts. The triple point is fixed at the origin, and the domain is truncated at a finite distance. Euler--Lagrange coordinates are employed to transform the unknown contact discontinuity curve (slip line) into a fixed boundary and to write the full Euler system as a first-order elliptic system for the flow direction and pressure coupled to transport equations for the Bernoulli and entropy quantities. The key idea in dealing with the contact discontinuity is to solve a mixed boundary value problem, in divergence form with discontinuous coefficients, for a single elliptic equation, so that continuity of the scalar unknown and its conormal flux allows reconstruction of the flow direction and pressure with the required contact discontinuity conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jun Chen, Xuemei Deng, Xiaoguang You

item.title: Quantitative Stability Of Aggregation-Diffusion Under Local Attraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.07264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we establish quantitative stability of aggregation-diffusion energy for compactly supported data. Our consideration focuses on the degenerate diffusion with local attraction that are asymptotically flat at infinity, such as Riesz kernels. We characterize the spectral gap of the Wasserstein Hessian at steady states.
item.dc:creator: Yunhong Deng

item.title: A Kinetic Concentration criterion for Large-data Boltzmann Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.12093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a conditional theory of genuinely non-perturbative global dynamics for the cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials on the three-dimensional torus. We prove that any global mild solution satisfying \[ \sup_{t\ge0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}W(v)\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3}F(t,x,v)\,dv<\infty, \] for a suitable stretched-exponential weight \(W\), enjoys uniform weighted \(L^\infty\) control, is unique in the dissipative mild class, and converges exponentially to the global Maxwellian. In particular, these conclusions hold for arbitrary-amplitude solutions admitting a uniform stretched-exponential velocity upper bound. The key mechanism is a *tail-to-coercivity principle*: uniform velocity-tail control generates positive lower bounds for the local density and nonlinear collision frequency, without imposing macroscopic coercivity a priori. A double-Duhamel positivity argument also generates a Gaussian lower bound at arbitrarily short positive times, allowing initial data with local vacuum. We establish a polynomially weighted counterpart under an additional spatially uniform lower velocity profile, obtaining analogous weighted \(L^\infty\) bounds, uniqueness, and exponential relaxation. Our results provide a low-regularity alternative to conditional theories requiring smoothness and pointwise macroscopic bounds. They reveal how a single velocity-tail condition controls large-data Boltzmann dynamics and suggest a route toward problems with physical boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Lingbing He, Jin-Cheng Jiang, Jong-In Kim, Donghyun Lee, Sungbin Park

item.title: Near-boundary rigidity and strict maximum modulus for Neumann eigenfunctions on convex planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.18546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a near-boundary rigidity theorem for arbitrary nonzero Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded convex planar domains. Precisely, if an eigenfunction $u$ with positive eigenvalue $\mu$ has an interior maximum-modulus point $p$ satisfying $\sqrt\mu\,\text{dist}(p,\partial\Omega)\le\pi/\sqrt3$, then $\Omega$ must be a rectangle and $u$ must be a cosine of one coordinate, and $\mu\ge4\mu_2(\Omega)$, with the factor $4$ being sharp. This shows that a scale-invariant distance condition at just one maximum-modulus point determines the geometry of the entire domain and the explicit form of the eigenfunction. We further prove that the maximum modulus of every second Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded convex planar domain is attained only on the boundary, without assuming boundary smoothness or eigenvalue simplicity. Moreover, we also prove strict boundary maximum modulus for higher Neumann eigenfunctions under suitable conditions, including all third Neumann eigenfunctions on arbitrary triangles.
item.dc:creator: Haiyun Deng, Xuyong Jiang, Xiaoping Yang

item.title: Uniform estimates for elliptic systems with critical Sobolev coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22366v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The elliptic regularity theory with $W^{1,n}$ coefficients dates back to Miranda, who established $W^{2,2}$ estimates for elliptic equations in divergence and non-divergence forms. For any such fixed operator, the $L^p$ estimates for all $1<p<\infty$ follow from the theory of VMO coefficients developed since the 1990s. However, the VMO theory does not yield constants in the estimates uniformly controlled by the $W^{1,n}$ norm of the coefficients, since the total $W^{1,n}$ norm does not control the VMO modulus. In this work, we establish uniform estimates for divergence-form elliptic systems with coefficients in the critical Sobolev--Lorentz spaces $W^{1,(n,s)}$ with $1\le s<\infty$, allowing an unbounded spatially skew-symmetric part. The constants in the estimates depend quantitatively on the critical Sobolev norms, and we show that they are sharp for scalar equations when $p>n$ and for systems when $p\neq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Tian Lan

item.title: On the stabilizing effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25694v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with a vanishing normal component, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Okazaki

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
item.description: arXiv:2610.32707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].
item.dc:creator: Wei Ji, Yixing Pu

item.title: Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.33689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\sigma<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$. We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[ \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-\Delta)^{\sigma/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $\sigma>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $\sigma=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.
item.dc:creator: Chang Liu

item.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39666v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$T(\Omega)\ge\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_\Omega\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)^2\,\mathrm{d} x,$$ where $T(\Omega)=4\int\limits_\Omega u\,\mathrm{d} x$ and $-\Delta u=1$ in $\Omega$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Equality holds for balls.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39794v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $(N-1)(k-1)+1$, and this bound $N$ for the second Dirichlet eigenvalue is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Chen, Chen-Gang Long, Shihong Zhang

item.title: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry
item.description: arXiv:1704.05790v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole -approaching a sub-extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om background fast enough at infinity- in presence of a massive and charged scalar field, motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in that setting : 1. Stability : We prove that spherically symmetric characteristic initial data to the Einstein-Maxwell- Klein-Gordon equations approaching a Reissner-Nordstr\"om background with a sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon in a neighbourhood of time-like infinity. Moreover if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. This generalizes the celebrated stability result of Dafermos for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. 2. Instability : We prove that for the class of space-times considered in the stability part, whose scalar field in addition obeys a polynomial averaged-L^2 (consistent) lower bound on the event horizon, the scalar field obeys an integrated lower bound transversally to the Cauchy horizon. As a consequence we prove that the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. This generalizes an instability result due to Luk and Oh for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. This instability of the black hole interior can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Van de Moortel

item.title: Mass inflation and the $C^2$-inextendibility of spherically symmetric charged scalar field dynamical black holes
item.description: arXiv:2001.11156v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has long been suggested that the Cauchy horizon of dynamical black holes is subject to a weak null singularity, under the mass inflation scenario. We study in spherical symmetry the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations and \textit{while we do not directly show mass inflation}, we obtain a "mass inflation/ridigity" dichotomy. More precisely, we prove assuming (sufficiently slow) decay of the charged scalar field on the event horizon, that the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}= \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$ for two (possibly empty) disjoint connected sets $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{S}$ such that: _$\mathcal{D}$ (the dynamical set) is a past set on which the Hawking mass blows up (mass inflation scenario). _$\mathcal{S}$ (the static set) is a future set isometric to a Reissner--Nordstr\"{o}m Cauchy horizon i.e.\ the radiation is zero on $\mathcal{S}$. As a consequence, we establish a novel classification of Cauchy horizons into three types: dynamical ($\mathcal{S}=\emptyset$), static ($\mathcal{D}=\emptyset$) or mixed, and prove that $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}$ is globally $C^2$-inextendible. Our main motivation is the $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture for a realistic model of spherical collapse in which charged matter emulates the repulsive role of angular momentum: in our case the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon system on one-ended space-times. As a result, we prove in spherical symmetry that: - two-ended asymptotically flat space-times are $C^2$-future-inextendible i.e. $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship is true for Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon, assuming the decay of the scalar field on the event horizon at the expected rate. - In the one-ended case, the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $C^2$-inextendible. This result suppresses the main obstruction to $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship in spherical collapse.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Van de Moortel

item.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2509.02239v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
item.dc:creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Prashanth Raman

item.title: On the Structure of Stationary Solutions to McKean-Vlasov Equations with Applications to Noisy Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2510.20094v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study stationary solutions of McKean-Vlasov equations on the circle. We establish an exact equivalence between solutions of the stationary McKean-Vlasov equation and an infinite-dimensional quadratic system of equations over Fourier coefficients, allowing explicit characterization of stationary states in a sequence space rather than a function space. This framework provides a transparent description of local bifurcations, their periodicity and resonance structures, while accommodating singular potentials. We derive analytic expressions for the emergence, form and shape (supercritical, critical, subcritical or transcritical) of bifurcations involving possibly multiple Fourier modes and connect them with discontinuous phase transitions. We also characterize, under suitable assumptions, the detailed structure of the stationary bifurcating solutions through leading small-amplitude coefficients for arbitrarily many fixed Fourier modes. At the global level, we establish regularity and concavity properties of the free energy landscape, proving existence, compactness, and coexistence of globally minimizing stationary measures, and identifying discontinuous phase transitions with points of non-differentiability of the minimum free energy map. We apply the theory to the Noisy Mean-Field Transformer model, where we show how changing the inverse temperature $\beta$ affects the geometry of the infinitely many bifurcations from the uniform measure. We also discuss how increasing $\beta$ motivates the study of approximate multi-mode stationary profiles as candidates for a separate metastability analysis; persistence times require additional dynamical estimates. Moreover, we determine the exact threshold $\beta_0\simeq2.447$ separating continuous and discontinuous phase transitions in this model. The same threshold marks the change of the first bifurcation from supercritical to subcritical.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Sayan Banerjee, Philippe Rigollet

item.title: A modified Consensus-Based Optimization model: consensus formation and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos
item.description: arXiv:2511.19116v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a modified CBO model based on a regularized Gibbs weight. For each fixed temperature and regularization parameter, the regularized weight yields a configuration-independent lower bound on the denominator of the consensus map, thus a quantitative analysis without an upper bound on the objective function or cutoff in the noise. We first prove large-time consensus for the finite-particle system: above an explicit stability threshold, every particle converges exponentially to a common random limit. This consensus mechanism does not require the $C^2$ condition used in the direct weighted-energy argument. We next prove uniform-in-time propagation of chaos: we derive quantitative bounds for the finite-particle consensus point from finite-time concentration estimates for the mean-field law, with explicit approximation and large-time tail errors. The synchronous-coupling estimate also gives a quantitative comparison between the random particle consensus point and the deterministic mean-field consensus point. We also quantify the regularization error in the quantitative Laplace principle, making the effect of the additive regularization explicit. A direct weighted-energy estimate is obtained under stronger $C^2$ assumptions. Furthermore, we give a stopped quadratic stability estimate with the actual Gibbs denominator. Under the weak-landscape condition, full support of the initial law, and local nondegeneracy of the minimizer, we prove a high-probability finite-particle global-optimization theorem for any fixed $\lambda>\sigma^2$. The proof combines an affine-flow local-mass estimate, finite-time mean-field entrance, ordinary finite-horizon propagation of chaos, and an $\alpha$-independent convex trapping energy near the minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Young-Pil Choi, Seungchan Lee, Sihyun Song

item.title: Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2512.17736v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Uniqueness for stochastic PDEs with drift in differential form is a main open problem in the recent literature on regularisation by noise. This paper establishes a self-contained theory in the framework of stochastic evolution equations on separable Hilbert spaces and provides a first result to address such an issue, in the direction of both pathwise and weak uniqueness, as well as continuous dependence on the initial data. The singularity of the drift allows to achieve novel uniqueness results for several classes of examples, ranging from fluid-dynamics to phase-separation models.
item.dc:creator: Davide Addona, Davide Bignamini, Carlo Orrieri, Luca Scarpa

item.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Picard-Type Operator Learning in Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2605.10277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Operator learning for partial differential equations (PDEs) aims to learn solution operators on infinite-dimensional function spaces from finite-resolution data. In this setting, it is important for the learned model to be discretization-invariant, or resolution-robust, and to reflect PDE-specific structure. It is therefore natural to ask how such structure should be encoded in the model architecture, hypothesis class, or learning procedure. In this paper, we study operator learning for solution operators of nonlinear parabolic PDEs based on Duhamel--Picard iteration. We formulate Picard iteration as an abstract state-transition model and present a theoretical framework for Picard-type operator learning. We derive implementation-agnostic generalization error bounds that separate the implementation error from the estimation error associated with the abstract state-transition model induced by Picard iteration. A key consequence is that increasing the Picard depth reduces the Picard truncation error without causing an unbounded growth of the entropy-based estimation error. We also extend the analysis to long-time prediction by rolling out the same learned local model over successive time blocks. Finally, we illustrate the theory for nonlinear heat equations on the torus using a Picard-type Fourier neural operator as a concrete implementation.
item.dc:creator: Koichi Taniguchi, Sho Sonoda

item.title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps
item.description: arXiv:2605.16747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a quantitative statistical theory of transformers in the large-context regime by adopting the abstraction of contextual flow maps (CFMs): dynamical systems that evolve a distinguished token in the presence of a contextual measure across a stack of attention blocks. Within this framework, the finite-context model approximates an idealized infinite-context system in which the contextual measure is replaced by its underlying population, so that the context length $n$ becomes a statistical resource. Exploiting the McKean--Vlasov structure of the dynamics and the classical machinery of propagation of chaos, we establish a forward bound controlling the deviation between the finite- and infinite-context CFMs uniformly along depth, and a backward bound controlling the deviation between the corresponding training trajectories uniformly across iterations of online gradient descent. Both bounds achieve the optimal Wasserstein rate $n^{-1/d}$ for general CFMs and parametric rate $n^{-1/2}$ for a restricted class of CFMs that includes transformers as a special case. The analysis rests on a new Eulerian adjoint formulation of the loss gradient and stability estimates for the resulting forward--adjoint system, both of which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Shi Chen, Zhengjiang Lin, Kaizhao Liu, Philippe Rigollet

item.title: Inequalities between Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues in large dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2606.30120v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain in $R^d$. Denote by $\lambda_k$ (resp. $\mu_k$) the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator in $\Omega$ with Dirichlet (resp. Neumann) boundary conditions. Denote by $\Psi = \Psi (d,k,\Omega)$ the shift of indices in the inequality $\mu_{k+\Psi} \le \lambda_k$. We are interested to describe the behaviour of $\Psi$ for large $d$. We prove that a) $\Psi (d,1,\Omega) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all domains $\Omega$; and b) $\Psi (d,k,\Omega) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all $k$ and all convex domains $\Omega$.
item.dc:creator: N. Filonov

item.title: Compatibility of Martensitic Microstructures in Polycrystals
item.description: arXiv:2607.12572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper studies martensitic microstructures in polycrystals, focussing on their compatibility across grain boundaries. After a reduction to the case of a planar grain boundary, the case when the grain boundary separates two constant gradients of zero energy is considered. It is shown that for cubic-to tetragonal transformations such a configuration can occur when the relative grain rotation is not in the cubic group. Then the case when the grain boundary separates two simple laminates of zero energy is considered, it being shown using a computer-assisted symbolic calculation that in the cubic-to-tetragonal case compatibility is only possible for a closed set of measure zero in the manifold of grain boundary normals and relative grain rotations, and that a similar slightly weaker result holds for cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations. The results suggest why higher-order laminates are often observed for such transformations. The Taylor set of deformation gradients is defined and studied, this set having the property that any deformation whose gradient belongs to it corresponds to a zero-energy microstructure for the polycrystal independent of grain geometry and grain rotations. New upper bounds for the Taylor set are proved for cubic-to-tetragonal and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations, generalizing those of Bhattacharya and Kohn using the geometrically linearized theory. We give a simple proof of a related result of Peigney characterizing the positive diagonal matrices in the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells for cubic-to-tetragonal transformations.
item.dc:creator: John M. Ball, Myrto Galanopoulou

item.title: Free boundary minimal annuli in convex balls
item.description: arXiv:2608.14679v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a $4$-parameter family of properly embedded genus-zero surfaces with at most two boundary components in a Riemannian $3$-ball. The construction is a free boundary analog of the canonical $5$-parameter family of surfaces on the $3$-sphere by Marques-Neves in the proof of Willmore conjecture. In the Euclidean unit ball, this family realizes the critical catenoid as a Simon-Smith min-max limit. As applications, we give an upper bound of Almgren-Pitts $4$-width $\omega_4(\mathbb{B}^3)$ by the area of the critical catenoid. Moreover, we prove the existence of at least three free boundary minimal annuli in any compact $3$-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature and strictly convex boundary.
item.dc:creator: Dongyeong Ko, Guanhua Shao

item.title: Excitation and Identifiability in the 2D Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.31230v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Convergence in parameter estimation classically requires ``persistency of excitation," which is a non-degeneracy condition on a trajectory-dependent signal. To the best of our knowledge, this paper develops the first such excitation theory for a nonlinear PDE. In the context of identifying the unknown viscosity from spectral observations in the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations for incompressible fluids, our excitation condition is computable, verifiable a priori, and sharp with respect to scaling. Our approach employs a data assimilation methodology to account for an unknown initial state and select candidate viscosities by minimizing the loss between the observed low-modes of the fluid velocity and low-modes of a nudging-based filter assimilating these observations. The main novelty of our framework is to distinguish a new functional, $\mathsf{W}$, representing the work done by the filter's associated sensitivity variable on the enstrophy, around which our entire analysis is centered. We show that $\mathsf{W}$ is explicitly comparable to the observability Gramian of the associated Gauss--Newton iteration, and subsequently establish the following dichotomy at every critical point of the observational loss: either $\mathsf{W}$ exceeds a minimal excitation threshold, in which case the candidate viscosity obeys an explicit error estimate that depends inversely on $\mathsf{W}$ and the observational density $N$, but directly on the error between initial conditions, or else the observations are quantitatively insensitive to parameter updates in a way that is detectable to the user. Our approach is energy-based, and therefore expected to be adaptable to many other nonlinear dissipative systems.
item.dc:creator: Vincent R. Martinez, Sarah Strikwerda, Xiang Wan

item.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.12238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $\Sigma_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_m)\to 4\pi^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Caniato

item.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31099v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{it\Delta}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Yongrui Tang
